title: EMPLOYMENT INSURANCE ACT
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to contribute to economic and social development through the implementation of employment insurance by preventing unemployment, promoting employment, developing and improving the vocational abilities of employees, etc., strengthening the State's vocational guidance and job placement functions, and, when employees, etc. become unemployed, providing benefits necessary for their livelihood to promote their livelihood security and job-seeking activities. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2008; Jan. 27, 2010; Jun. 4, 2010; Jul. 21, 2011; May 26, 2020; Jan. 5, 2021>
  1. "Insured person" means any of the following persons:
  a. An employee, artist, or personal work performer who is insured or deemed insured under Articles 5(1) and (2), 6(1), 8(1) and (2), 48-2(1), and 48-3(1) of the Act on the Collection of Insurance Premiums for Employment Insurance and Industrial Accident Co mpensation Insurance (hereinafter referred to as "Insurance Premium Collection Act"); 자
  b. A self-employed person who is insured or deemed insured under Article 49-2(1) and (2) of the Insurance Premium Collection Act (hereinafter referred to as "insured self-employed person");
  2. “Separation from employment” means the termination of the employment relationship between an insured person and a business owner (or, in cases of artists under Article 77-2(1) or personal work performers under Article 77-6(1), the termination of a contract related to culture and arts services or a contract for personal work);
  3. "Unemployment" means the state of being unable to obtain employment despite having the willingness and ability to work;
  4. "Recognition of unemployment" means recognition by the head of an employment security office that an eligible recipient under Article 43 is unemployed and is actively seeking employment;
  5. “Remuneration” means the amount calculated by subtracting money and valuables prescribed by Presidential Decree from earned income under Article 20 of the Income Tax Act; provided, money and valuables determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Employment and Labor, of the money and valuables received from a person other than a business owner during a period of leave of absence or any other similar period, shall be construed as remuneration;
  6. “Daily employee” means a person employed for less than 1 month.

Article 3 (Administration of insurance) Employment insurance (hereinafter referred to as “insurance”) shall be administered by the Minister of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 4 (Employment insurance programs) (1) In order to achieve the purpose under Article 1, employment insurance shall operate employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs, unemployment benefits, child care leave benefits, maternity leave benefits, etc. as employment insurance programs (hereinafter referred to as “insurance programs”). <Amended on Feb. 1, 2012>
  (2) The insurance year for insurance programs shall coincide with the Government’s fiscal year.

Article 5 (Bearing of costs by the State) (1) The State shall bear, from the general account, part of the costs incurred in insurance programs each year. <Amended on Jan. 20, 2015>
  (2) The State may, within the budget, bear the costs incurred each year in the management and operation of insurance programs.

Article 6 (Insurance premiums) (1) Insurance premiums and other amounts collectible to cover the costs incurred in insurance programs under this Act shall be governed by the Insurance Premium Collection Act. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>
  (2) Insurance premiums for employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs and insurance premiums for unemployment benefits, collected under Article 13(1)1 of the Insurance Premium Collection Act, shall be appropriated to cover the costs incurred in the respective programs; provided, insurance premiums for unemployment benefits may be appropriated to cover expenses incurred in subsidizing National Pension contributions under Article 55-2(1), paying child care leave benefits under Article 70(1), paying benefits for reduced working hours during periods of child care under Article 73-2(1), paying maternity leave benefits, etc. under Articles 75 and 76-2, and paying maternity benefits, etc. under Articles 77-4 and 77-9. <Amended on Feb. 1, 2012; Jan. 15, 2019; Jan. 5, 2021>
  (3) Notwithstanding paragraph (2), insurance premiums for employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs and insurance premiums for unemployment benefits, collected from insured self-employed persons under Article 49-2 of the Insurance Premium Collection Act, shall be appropriated to cover the costs incurred in the respective programs for insured self-employed persons; provided, insurance premiums for unemployment benefits may be appropriated to cover expenses incurred in subsidizing National Pension contributions under Article 55-2(1) for insured self-employed persons. <Added on Jul. 21, 2011; Jan. 15, 2019; Jan. 5, 2021>

Article 7 (Employment Insurance Committee) (1) The Employment Insurance Committee (hereafter in this Article referred to as the “Committee”) shall be established in the Ministry of Employment and Labor to deliberate on important matters relating to the enforcement of this Act and the Insurance Premium Collection Act (limited to matters relating to insurance). <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010; Jan. 5, 2021>
  (2) The Committee shall deliberate on the following matters: <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>
  1. Matters relating to the improvement of the insurance system and insurance programs;
  2. Matters relating to the determination of insurance premium rates under the Insurance Premium Collection Act;
  3. Matters relating to the evaluation of insurance programs under Article 11-2;
  4. Matters relating to the formulation of plans for operating the Fund and the results of the operation of the Fund under Article 81;
  5. Other matters deemed by the chairperson to require deliberation by the Committee in relation to the insurance system and insurance programs.
  (3) The Committee shall be comprised of not more than 20 members, including 1 chairperson.
  (4) The Vice Minister of Employment and Labor shall serve as the chairperson of the Committee, and its members shall be appointed or commissioned by the Minister of Employment and Labor in equal numbers from among the following persons: <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  1. Persons representing employees;
  2. Persons representing employers;
  3. Persons representing the public interest;
  4. Persons representing the Government.
  (5) The Committee may establish a specialized committee in the Committee to review and coordinate matters subject to deliberation in advance.
  (6) The composition and operation of the Committee and specialized committees and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 8 (Scope of application) (1) This Act shall apply to every business or workplace that employs employees (hereinafter referred to as a “business”); provided, this Act shall not apply to businesses prescribed by Presidential Decree in consideration of industry-specific characteristics, size, etc. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>
  (2) This Act shall apply to businesses that receive services from artists under Article 77-2(1) or personal work performers under Article 77-6(1); provided, the provisions of Chapters I, II, IV, V-2, V-3, VI, VIII, or IX relating to artists or personal work performers shall apply, respectively. <Added on Jan. 5, 2021; Dec. 31, 2022>>

Article 9 (Establishment or termination of insurance relationship) The establishment and termination of an insurance relationship under this Act shall be governed by the Insurance Premium Collection Act. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>

Article 10 (Exclusion from application) (1) This Act shall not apply to any of the following persons: <Amended on Mar. 21, 2008; Dec. 11, 2012; Jun. 4, 2013; Jan. 15, 2019; May 26, 2020; Dec. 31, 2022>
  1. Deleted; <Jan. 15, 2019>
  2. An employee whose prescribed working hours in the relevant business are less than the hours prescribed by Presidential Decree;
  3. A public official under the State Public Officials Act or the Local Public Officials Act; provided, public officials in extraordinary civil service and public officials in fixed term positions under Article 26-5 of the State Public Officials Act and Article 25-5 of the Local Public Officials Act may be insured under employment insurance (limited to Chapter IV) at their own request, as prescribed by Presidential Decree;
  4. A person subject to the Pension for Private School Teachers and Staff Act;
  5. Any other person prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) Chapters IV and V shall not apply to a person who is employed after attaining the age of 65 (excluding a person who continues to be employed after attaining the age of 65 while maintaining insured status before attaining the age of 65) or who commences self-employment after attaining the age of 65. <Added on Jan. 15, 2019>
  [Title Amended on Jun. 4, 2013]

Article 10-2 (Application to foreign employees, artists, and personal work performers) (1) This Act shall apply to foreign workers to whom the Act on the Employment of Foreign Workers applies; provided, Chapters IV and V shall apply only upon an application filed as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor.
  (2) If a foreigner, other than a foreign worker under paragraph (1), enters into an employment contract, a contract related to culture and arts services under Article 77-2(1), or a contract for personal work under Article 77-6(1), all or part of this Act shall apply as prescribed by Presidential Decree, taking into account the scope of activities, period of stay, etc. under the status of stay prescribed in Article 10 of the Immigration Act. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2022>
  [This Article Added on Jan. 15, 2019]
  [Title Amended on Dec. 31, 2022]

Article 11 (Insurance-related surveys and research) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor may conduct research on the labor market, occupations, and vocational skills development, and survey and research projects to support insurance-related affairs. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (2) If deemed necessary, the Minister of Employment and Labor may require a person prescribed by Presidential Decree to perform part of the affairs under paragraph (1) on behalf of the Minister. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 11-2 (Evaluation of insurance programs) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall conduct ongoing and systematic evaluations of insurance programs. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (2) In order to ensure the expertise of evaluations under paragraph (1), the Minister of Employment and Labor may commission an institution prescribed by Presidential Decree to conduct the evaluations under paragraph (1). <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (3) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall, based on the results of the evaluations under paragraphs (1) and (2), adjust insurance programs or formulate plans for operating the Fund under Article 81. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  [This Article Added on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 12 (International exchange and cooperation) The Minister of Employment and Labor may conduct exchange and cooperation programs with international organizations, foreign governments, or foreign institutions in relation to insurance programs. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

CHAPTER II MANAGEMENT OF INSURED PERSONS

Article 13 (Date of acquisition of insured status) (1) An insured person who is an employee shall acquire insured status on the date they are employed in a business to which this Act applies; provided, in any of the following cases, he or she shall be construed as having acquired insured status on the relevant date: <Amended on Jul. 21, 2011; Jan. 15, 2019; May 26, 2020; Jan. 5, 2021>
  1. Where an employee excluded from application under Articles 10 and 10-2 becomes subject to this Act: The date on which the employee becomes subject to this Act;
  2. In the case of an employee employed before the date on which an insurance relationship is established under Article 7 of the Insurance Premium Collection Act: The date on which such insurance relationship is established.
  (2) An insured self-employed person shall acquire insured status on the date on which an insurance relationship is established under Article 49-2(1) and subparagraph 3 of Article 7, as applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 49-2(12), of the Insurance Premium Collection Act. <Added on Jul. 21, 2011; Jan. 5, 2021>

Article 14 (Date of loss of insured status) (1) An insured person who is an employee shall lose insured status on any of the following dates: <Amended on Jul. 21, 2011; Jan. 15, 2019; Jan. 5, 2021>
  1. Where an insured person who is an employee becomes an employee excluded from application under Articles 10 and 10-2: The date on which the employee becomes excluded from application;
  2. Where an insurance relationship is terminated under Article 10 of the Insurance Premium Collection Act: The date on which such insurance relationship is terminated;
  3. Where an insured employee separates from employment: The day following the date of separation from employment;
  4. Where an insured employee dies: The date following the date of death.
  (2) An insured self-employed person shall lose insured status on the date on which an insurance relationship is terminated under Article 49-2(10) and subparagraphs 1 through 3 of Article 10, as applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 49-2(12), of the Insurance Premium Collection Act. <Added on Jul. 21, 2011; Jan. 5, 2021>

Article 15 (Reporting on insured status) (1) A business owner shall file a report with the Minister of Employment and Labor on matters relating to the acquisition and loss of insured status, etc. of employees employed in the relevant business, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (2) Where a primary contractor becomes the business owner under Article 9 of the Insurance Premium Collection Act, any of the following subcontractors employing employees engaged in the relevant business, other than those employed by the primary contractor, shall file a report under paragraph (1); in such cases, the primary contractor shall submit data on the subcontractors to the Minister of Employment and Labor, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor: <Amended on Feb. 4, 2010; Jun. 4, 2010; May 24, 2011; Jan. 19, 2016; Apr. 30, 2019; Jan. 5, 2021; Aug. 8, 2023>
  1. A constructor defined in subparagraph 7 of Article 2 of the Framework Act on the Construction Industry;
  2. A housing construction business operator under Article 4 of the Housing Act;
  3. A constructor defined in subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Electrical Construction Business Act;
  4. An information and communications construction business operator defined in subparagraph 4 of Article 2 of the Information and Communications Construction Business Act;
  5. A firefighting system business operator defined in Article 2(1)2 of the Firefighting System Installation Business Act;
  6. A national heritage repair business operator under Article 14 of the Act on National Heritage Maintenance.
  (3) If a business owner fails to file a report on matters relating to insured status under paragraph (1), an employee may file a report as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (4) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall notify insured persons, primary contractors, and other relevant persons of matters relating to the acquisition and loss of insured status, etc. reported under paragraphs (1) through (3), as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (5) A business owner, primary contractor, or subcontractor under paragraph (1) or (2) may file a report under that paragraph by electronic means prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (6) The Minister of Employment and Labor may provide a business owner, primary contractor, or subcontractor who intends to file a report by electronic means under paragraph (5) with necessary equipment, etc., as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (7) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), an insured self-employed person shall not file a report on the acquisition and loss of insured status. <Added on Jul. 21, 2011>

Article 16 Deleted. <Aug. 27, 2019>

Article 17 (Verification of insured status) (1) An insured person or a former insured person may request the Minister of Employment and Labor at any time to verify the acquisition or loss of insured status. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010; May 26, 2020>
  (2) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall verify the acquisition or loss of insured status upon a request under paragraph (1) or ex officio. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (3) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall notify the insured person who requested the verification, the business owner, and other relevant persons of the results of the verification under paragraph (2), as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 18 (Criteria for acquisition of insured status) (1) If an employee under subparagraph 1a of Article 2 is simultaneously employed in 2 or more businesses in which an insurance relationship has been established, he or she shall acquire insured status with respect to 1 of those businesses, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) A person who falls under both subparagraphs 1a and 1b of Article 2 shall acquire insured status as an employee, artist, or personal work performer under subparagraph 1a of Article 2; provided, if an insured person under subparagraph 1a of Article 2 falls under any of the following subparagraphs, he or she shall select either insured status under subparagraph 1a or insured status under subparagraph 1b of Article 2 and acquire or maintain such insured status:
  1. A daily employee;
  2. A short-term artist under the proviso of Article 77-2(2)2;
  3. A short-term personal work performer under the proviso of Article 77-6(2)2.
  (3) Notwithstanding paragraph (2), a person who falls under both subparagraph 1a and b of Article 2 may, at his or her option, acquire or maintain both insured statuses under items a and b of that subparagraph.
  (4) If an artist or personal work performer under subparagraph 1a of Article 2 simultaneously provides labor or work in 2 or more businesses in which an insurance relationship has been established, he or she shall acquire insured status, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2022]

CHAPTER III EMPLOYMENT STABILIZATION AND VOCATIONAL SKILLS DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS

Article 19 (Implementation of employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall implement employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs to prevent unemployment, promote employment, expand employment opportunities, provide and support opportunities for vocational skills development and improvement, and otherwise support employment stabilization and the securing of human resources by business owners for insured persons, former insured persons, and other persons seeking employment (hereinafter referred to as “insured persons, etc.”). <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010; May 26, 2020>
  (2) In implementing employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs under paragraph (1), the Minister of Employment and Labor shall give priority consideration to enterprises that satisfy standards prescribed by Presidential Decree, including the number of employees and measures taken and performance achieved for employment stabilization and vocational skills development (hereinafter referred to as “enterprises eligible for priority support”). <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010; Aug. 27, 2019>

Article 20 (Support for job creation) The Minister of Employment and Labor may, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, provide necessary support to a business owner who expands employment opportunities through improvements in the working environment, changes in work arrangements, etc.<Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 21 (Support for employment adjustment) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor may provide necessary support, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to a business owner for whom employment adjustment has become unavoidable due to a reduction in the scale of business, permanent closure of business, business conversion, or other causes resulting from economic fluctuations, changes in the industrial structure, etc., where the business owner requires employees not to provide labor through measures such as temporary closure of business or leave of absence, provides vocational skills development training necessary for career transition, reallocates personnel, or takes other measures for employment security. In such cases, where money and valuables paid by the business owner to employees are reduced to a level prescribed by Presidential Decree as a result of measures for employment security, the Minister may also provide necessary support to such employees, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010; Jan. 23, 2013; Aug. 27, 2019; Nov. 11, 2025>
  (2) The Minister of Employment and Labor may provide necessary support, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to a business owner who takes measures to stabilize employment for employees whose employment has become unstable, including employing employees separated from employment due to employment adjustment under paragraph (1). <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (3) In providing support under paragraph (1), the Minister of Employment and Labor may expand such support for a business owner or employee, as prescribed by Presidential Decree after deliberation by the Employment Policy Deliberative Council under Article 10 of the Framework Act on Employment Policy, in any of the following cases: <Amended on Oct. 9, 2009; Jun. 4, 2010; Jan. 23, 2013; Nov. 11, 2025>
  1. Where the business owner or employee is engaged in an industry or is located in an area under Article 32 of the Framework Act on Employment Policy;
  2. Where the nationwide employment situation has significantly deteriorated and special support has become necessary.

Article 22 (Promotion of local employment) The Minister of Employment and Labor may provide necessary support, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to a business owner who has contributed to preventing unemployment and promoting reemployment in a region where employment opportunities are substantially insufficient or where the employment situation is rapidly deteriorating due to changes in the industrial structure or other causes, by relocating a business to such region or establishing or expanding a business in such region, or to a business owner who has taken other measures necessary to expand employment opportunities in such region. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 23 (Support for employment promotion of the aged, etc.) The Minister of Employment and Labor may provide necessary support, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to a business owner who newly employs aged persons, etc. or takes measures necessary for their employment security in order to promote the employment of aged persons and other persons who have particular difficulty in obtaining employment under ordinary labor market conditions (hereinafter referred to as "the aged, etc."), or to employees covered by measures for employment security implemented by such business owner. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010; May 26, 2020>

Article 24 (Support for employment security of construction workers and other employees) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor may provide necessary support, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to business owners who implement the following programs for construction workers and other employees with unstable employment: <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  1. Programs for improving employment conditions;
  2. Programs for employment security, including the provision of continuous employment opportunities;
  3. Other programs for employment security prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) If it is difficult for a business owner to implement a program for employment security under any subparagraph of paragraph (1) independently, the Minister of Employment and Labor may also provide support to a business owners’ association in cases prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 25 (Employment security and employment promotion) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor may directly implement the following programs to promote employment security and facilitate the employment of insured persons, etc., or may provide subsidies or loans for expenses necessary for implementing such programs: <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  1. Programs to support improvement in employment management, such as employment management diagnosis;
  2. Support programs to promote business start-ups by insured persons, etc.;
  3. Other programs prescribed by Presidential Decree to promote employment security and facilitate the employment of insured persons, etc.
  (2) Matters necessary for implementing the programs and providing subsidies or loans for expenses under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 26 (Support for employment promotion facilities) To support employment security and employment promotion for insured persons, etc. and the securing of human resources by business owners, the Minister of Employment and Labor may provide necessary support, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to a person who establishes and operates counseling facilities, child care centers, or other employment promotion facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010; Jun. 7, 2011>

Article 26-2 (Restriction on support) When providing support under Articles 20 through 26, the Minister of Employment and Labor may provide such support after deducting the relevant amount in cases prescribed by Presidential Decree, including where a business owner has received money, such as subsidies or incentives, under other statutes or regulations.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 21, 2011]

Article 27 (Support for vocational skills development training provided by business owners) (1) To develop and improve the vocational skills of insured persons, etc., the Minister of Employment and Labor may, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, provide subsidies to cover expenses incurred in vocational skills development training prescribed by Presidential Decree and provided by a business owner. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010; Dec. 27, 2016>
  (2) The Minister of Employment and Labor may provide preferential support, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, where a business owner provides vocational skills development training under paragraph (1) to any of the following persons: <Added on Dec. 27, 2016; Apr. 30, 2019; Jan. 5, 2021>
  1. A fixed-term employee defined in subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Act on the Protection of Fixed-Term and Part-Time Employees;
  2. A part-time employee defined in Article 2(1)9 of the Labor Standards Act;
  3. A temporary agency worker defined in subparagraph 5 of Article 2 of the Act on the Protection of Temporary Agency Workers;
  4. A daily employee;
  5. An aged or middle-aged person defined in subparagraph 1 or 2 of Article 2 of the Act on Prohibition of Age Discrimination in Employment and Elderly Employment Promotion;
  6. Other persons prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 28 (Criteria for subsidization of expenses) If the Minister of Employment and Labor provides subsidies to cover expenses for a business owner under Article 27, the amount of such subsidies shall be the amount calculated by multiplying the insurance premiums for employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs included in the relevant year’s employment insurance premiums obtained by adding all monthly insurance premiums under Article 16-3 of the Insurance Premium Collection Act or the relevant year’s estimated employment insurance premiums under Article 17 of that Act, by the ratio prescribed by Presidential Decree, and the limit thereof shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jan. 27, 2010; Jun. 4, 2010; Jan. 5, 2021>

Article 29 (Support for vocational skills development of insured persons, etc.) (1) If insured persons, etc. receive vocational skills development training or otherwise endeavor to develop and improve their vocational skills, the Minister of Employment and Labor may provide subsidies to cover the necessary expenses, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (2) If deemed necessary, the Minister of Employment and Labor may conduct vocational skills development training to promote the employment of insured persons, etc., as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (3) If low-income insured persons, etc. prescribed by Presidential Decree receive vocational skills development training, the Minister of Employment and Labor may extend loans for living expenses, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added on Dec. 31, 2008; Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 30 (Support for vocational skills development training facilities) If the Minister of Employment and Labor deems it necessary to develop and improve the vocational skills of insured persons, etc., the Minister may extend loans for expenses necessary for establishing vocational skills development training facilities and purchasing equipment, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, and may subsidize expenses determined by the Minister as necessary for establishing vocational skills development training facilities and purchasing and operating equipment. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 31 (Promotion of vocational skills development) (1) To promote the development and improvement of vocational skills of insured persons, etc., the Minister of Employment and Labor may implement the following programs or provide subsidies to persons who implement such programs to cover expenses necessary for implementing such programs: <Amended on May 31, 2010; Jun. 4, 2010>
  1. Programs for technical support for, and evaluation of, vocational skills development programs;
  2. Qualification testing programs and programs to promote skilled crafts under the Act on Encouragement of Skilled Crafts;
  3. Other programs prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) If deemed necessary to develop and improve vocational skills and to facilitate the supply of and demand for human resources, the Minister of Employment and Labor may entrust vocational skills development training programs for occupations determined by the Minister of Employment and Labor to be implemented, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 32 (Support for vocational skills development of construction workers) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor may provide subsidies to business owners who implement programs prescribed by Presidential Decree as programs for developing and improving vocational skills for construction workers and other employees with unstable employment to cover expenses necessary for implementing such programs. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (2) In cases prescribed by Presidential Decree where it is difficult for a business owner to independently implement a vocational skills development program in connection with the programs under paragraph (1), the Minister of Employment and Labor may also provide support to a business owners’ association. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 33 (Provision of employment information and establishment of foundation for employment support) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor may implement programs for providing business owners and insured persons, etc. with employment information, such as information on job openings, job search, and training, and with vocational guidance, such as counseling on occupations and training, providing job placement, establishing foundations for employment stabilization and vocational skills development, and placing specialized personnel necessary therefor. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (2) If deemed necessary, the Minister of Employment and Labor may require private employment counselors under Article 4-4 of the Employment Security Act to perform part of the affairs under paragraph (1). <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 34 (Support for local governments) The Minister of Employment and Labor may provide necessary support, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to a local government or a non-profit corporation or organization prescribed by Presidential Decree that implements programs for employment security, employment promotion, and vocational skills development for insured persons, etc. in the relevant region. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 35 (Restriction on support due to improper acts) (1) With respect to a person who has received or seeks to receive support for employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs under this Chapter by fraud or other improper means, the Minister of Employment and Labor shall not pay the unpaid amount of the relevant subsidy or the subsidy sought, shall restrict the payment of subsidies for a period prescribed by Presidential Decree within 1 year, and shall order the return of the amount received by fraud or other improper means. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2008; Jun. 4, 2010; Jan. 20, 2015>
  (2) In issuing an order for return under paragraph (1), the Minister of Employment and Labor may additionally collect an amount not exceeding 5 times the amount received by fraud or other improper means, in accordance with the standards prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2008; Jun. 4, 2010>
  (3) If a subsidy has been erroneously paid to a person who has received support for employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs, the Minister of Employment and Labor may order the return thereof. <Added on Aug. 27, 2019>
  (4) Notwithstanding paragraphs (1) and (2), Articles 55 and 56 of the National Lifelong Vocational Skills Development Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the restriction of support, return, and additional collection with respect to a person who has received or seeks to receive support for vocational skills development programs by fraud or other improper means. <Added on Dec. 31, 2008; May 31, 2010; Aug. 27, 2019; Jan. 5, 2021; Aug. 17, 2021>
  (5) The Minister of Employment and Labor may deny support for employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs under this Chapter to a person who is in arrears on insurance premiums, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2008; Jun. 4, 2010; Jul. 21, 2011; Aug. 27, 2019>
  [Article 35(1) is amended on Jan. 20, 2015 (Act No. 13041) in accordance with the Constitutional Court's decision of Aug. 29, 2013, declaring the previous Article 35(1) unconstitutional]

Article 36 (Performance of affairs on behalf of the Minister) The Minister of Employment and Labor may, if deemed necessary, have a person prescribed by Presidential Decree perform part of the affairs under Articles 19,27 through 31 on behalf of the Minister. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

CHAPTER IV UNEMPLOYMENT BENEFITS

SECTION 1 General Provisions

Article 37 (Types of unemployment benefits) (1) Unemployment benefits shall be classified into job-seeking benefits and employment promotion allowances.
  (2) The types of employment promotion allowances shall be as follows:
  1. Early re-employment allowance;
  2. Vocational skills development allowance;
  3. Long-distance job search allowance;
  4. Relocation allowance.

Article 37-2 (Account for the receipt of unemployment benefits) (1) Upon an application by an eligible recipient under Article 43, the head of an employment security office shall deposit unemployment benefits into a designated account in the name of the eligible recipient (hereinafter referred to as an “account for the receipt of unemployment benefits”); provided, if unemployment benefits cannot be transferred to the account for the receipt of unemployment benefits due to an information and communications failure or any other unavoidable reason prescribed by Presidential Decree, the head of the employment security office may pay unemployment benefits in cash or by any other method as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) The financial institution maintaining the account for the receipt of unemployment benefits shall manage the account so that only unemployment benefits under this Act are deposited into the account.
  (3) Matters necessary for the methods and procedures for applications under paragraph (1) and for the management of accounts for the receipt of unemployment benefits under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Jan. 20, 2015]

Article 38 (Protection of entitlement to benefits) (1) No right to receive unemployment benefits may be transferred, seized, or pledged. <Amended on Jan. 20, 2015>
  (2) No claim to the amount not exceeding the amount prescribed by Presidential Decree, among deposits in the account for the receipt of unemployment benefits designated under Article 37-2(1) may be seized. <Added on Jan. 20, 2015>

Article 38-2 (Exemption from public charges) No public charges imposed by the State or a local government (referring to public charges defined in subparagraph 8 of Article 2 of the Framework Act on National Taxes or Article 2(1)26 of the Framework Act on Local Taxes) shall be imposed on money and valuables paid as unemployment benefits.
  [This Article Added on Mar. 22, 2013]

Article 39 Deleted. <Jun. 4, 2013>

SECTION 2 Job-Seeking Benefits

Article 40 (Eligibility requirements for job-seeking benefits) (1) Job-seeking benefits shall be paid if an insured person who is an employee and has separated from employment satisfies all of the following requirements; provided, subparagraphs 5 and 6 shall apply only to a person who was a daily employee at the time of the most recent separation from employment: <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019; Aug. 27, 2019; May 26, 2020; Jan. 5, 2021; Dec. 31, 2022; Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. The aggregate number of qualifying days in covered employment (referring to qualifying days in covered employment under Article 41; hereinafter the same shall apply) during the base period under paragraph (2) (hereinafter referred to as the "base period") shall be at least 180 days;
  2. The insured person shall be in a state of being unable to obtain employment, despite having the willingness and ability to work (including conducting business for profit; hereafter in this Chapter and Chapter V the same shall apply);
  3. The reason for separation from employment shall not fall under any ground for restriction on eligibility under Article 58;
  4. The insured person shall actively seek re-employment;
  5. The insured person shall fall under any of the following items:
  a. The aggregate number of working days from the first day of the month immediately preceding the month in which the date of application for recognition of eligibility for benefits under Article 43 falls to the date of application for recognition of eligibility for benefits shall be less than 1/3 of the total number of days during that period;
  b. The insured person shall be a daily employee in the construction industry (referring to a daily employee who was engaged, at the time of separation from employment, in the Construction Section of the Korean Standard Industrial Classification publicly notified by the Minister of Data and Statistics under Article 22(1) of the Statistics Act; hereinafter the same shall apply) and shall have no record of work for 14 consecutive days before the date of application for recognition of eligibility for benefits;
  6. Where, among the qualifying days in covered employment during the base period at the time of the most recent separation from employment, the insured person has separated from employment in another business for a reason falling under any ground for restriction on eligibility under Article 58, he or she shall have worked as a daily employee for at least 90 days during such qualifying days in covered employment.
  (2) The base period shall be 18 months preceding the date of separation from employment; provided, if an insured employee falls under any of the following cases, the base period shall be the period specified in the relevant subparagraph: <Amended on Aug. 27, 2019; Jan. 5, 2021>
  1. Where the insured employee was unable to receive remuneration for at least 30 consecutive days during the 18-month period preceding the date of separation from employment due to illness, injury, or any other reason prescribed by Presidential Decree: The period obtained by adding to 18 months the number of days during which he or she was unable to receive remuneration due to such reason (if the period exceeds 3 years, it shall be 3 years);
  2. Where all of the following requirements are satisfied: The 24-month period preceding the date of separation from employment:
  a. The insured employee shall have worked as an employee whose prescribed working hours per week were less than 15 hours and whose prescribed working days per week were 2 days or less at the time of separation from employment;
  b. The insured employee shall have worked as an employee satisfying the requirements under item a for at least 90 days during the qualifying days in covered employment within the 24-month period preceding the date of separation from employment.

Article 41 (Qualifying days in covered employment) (1) The qualifying days in covered employment of an employee shall be calculated by aggregating the days based on which remuneration was paid during the period of covered employment; provided, the qualifying days in covered employment of an insured self-employed person shall be the period of covered employment under the proviso of Article 50(3) and Article 50(4). <Amended on Jan. 27, 2010; Jul. 21, 2011; Jan. 5, 2021>
  (2) In calculating qualifying days in covered employment under paragraph (1), if a person has received job-seeking benefits before the date on which he or she most recently acquired insured status, the qualifying days in covered employment before the date of loss of insured status related to those job-seeking benefits shall not be included. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2008; Jan. 27, 2010; Jul. 21, 2011>
  (3) If an insured employee worked, during the base period under Article 40(2), as a person falling under at least 2 of the following: an employee, an artist under Article 77-2(1), or a personal work performer under Article 77-6(1), the qualifying days in covered employment shall be determined as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added on Jan. 5, 2021>

Article 42 (Reporting of unemployment) (1) A person who intends to receive job-seeking benefits shall, without delay after separation from employment, appear at an employment security office and report his or her unemployment; provided, if there is a reason prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor, such as difficulty in appearing due to a disaster under subparagraph 1 of Article 3 of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety, he or she may file such report through the employment information system under Article 15-2 of the Framework Act on Employment Policy. <Amended on May 26, 2020; Dec. 31, 2022>
  (2) A report of unemployment under paragraph (1) shall include an application for registration as a job seeker and an application for recognition of eligibility for benefits under Article 43.
  (3) A person who intends to report his or her unemployment in order to receive job-seeking benefits under paragraph (1) may request the business owner of the business in which he or she was employed before separation from employment to issue materials verifying qualifying days in covered employment, prescribed working hours per day before separation from employment, etc. (hereinafter referred to as "certificate of separation from employment"). In such cases, the business owner upon receipt of such request shall issue a certificate of separation from employment, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Added on Aug. 27, 2019>

Article 43 (Recognition of eligibility for benefits) (1) A person who intends to receive job-seeking benefits shall apply to the head of an employment security office for recognition of eligibility for benefits under Article 40(1)1 through 3,5, and 6 (hereinafter referred to as "eligibility for benefits"). <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019; May 26, 2020>
  (2) Upon receipt of an application for recognition of eligibility for benefits under paragraph (1), the head of an employment security office shall determine whether the applicant is eligible for benefits and shall notify the applicant of the results, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) If an applicant under paragraph (2) satisfies all of the following requirements, eligibility for benefits shall be determined based on the business from which he or she most recently separated from employment; provided, if a person whose most recent separation from employment was as a daily employee and whose qualifying days in covered employment amount to less than 1 month is not eligible for benefits, eligibility for benefits shall be determined based on the business from which he or she most recently separated from employment as an employee other than a daily employee: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2008; May 26, 2020>
  1. Before being employed in the business from which he or she most recently separated from employment as an insured person, he or she had previously separated from employment as an insured person;
  2. He or she has not received job-seeking benefits in connection with any separation from employment before the most recent separation from employment.
  (4) If necessary to determine whether where an applicant is eligible for benefits under paragraphs (2) and (3), the head of an employment security office may request the business owner of the business in which the applicant was employed before separation from employment to submit a certificate of separation from employment, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. In such cases, the business owner who receives such request shall submit the certificate of separation from employment, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Added on Aug. 27, 2019>
  (5) If a person whose eligibility for benefits has been recognized under paragraph (2) (hereinafter referred to as an "eligible recipient") is newly recognized as eligible for benefits during the period under Article 48 or Article 54(1), job-seeking benefits shall be paid based on the newly recognized eligibility for benefits. <Amended on Aug. 27, 2019; May 26, 2020>

Article 43-2 (Recognition of eligibility for benefits when acquiring two or more insured statuses) (1) If an insured person, as an employee, an artist under Article 77-2(1), a personal work performer under Article 77-6(1), or an insured self-employed person, has acquired 2 or more different insured statuses and, upon separation from employment, has lost all such insured statuses, and seeks to receive job-seeking benefits, eligibility for benefits shall be determined based on the insured status selected by the person from among those statuses.
  (2) If the insured status selected by a person seeking recognition of eligibility for benefits under paragraph (1) is not the insured status most recently lost (where insured statuses are lost simultaneously, meaning all insured statuses so lost; hereafter in this paragraph the same shall apply), eligibility for benefits shall be recognized only if the reason for separation from employment related to the insured status most recently lost does not fall under any ground for restriction on eligibility for benefits under Article 58 or Article 69-7; provided, if the head of an employment security office recognizes that the separation from employment was due to a reduction in income as prescribed by Presidential Decree, such separation from employment shall be deemed not to fall under any ground for restriction on eligibility for benefits.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 31, 2022]

Article 44 (Recognition of unemployment) (1) Job-seeking benefits shall be paid for days on which an eligible recipient is in a state of unemployment and for which unemployment has been recognized by the head of an employment security office.
  (2) An eligible recipient seeking recognition of unemployment shall appear on a date designated by the head of an employment security office within a period of 1 week to 4 weeks beginning on the date on which he or she reported unemployment under Article 42 (hereinafter referred to as the "unemployment recognition date"), and shall report that he or she has made efforts to obtain reemployment, and the head of the employment security office shall recognize the eligible recipient as unemployed for each day from the day following the immediately preceding unemployment recognition date to the unemployment recognition date; provided, the method of recognition of unemployment for any of the following persons shall be governed by the standards prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor: <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010; May 26, 2020>
  1. An eligible recipient receiving vocational skills development training, etc.;
  2. An eligible recipient where a reason prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as a natural disaster or mass unemployment, has arisen;
  3. Other eligible recipients prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) Notwithstanding paragraph (2), if an eligible recipient falls under any of the following, he or she may obtain recognition of unemployment by submitting a certificate specifying the reason he or she was unable to appear at an employment security office:
  1. Where he or she was unable to appear at an employment security office due to illness or injury and the period thereof was less than 7 consecutive days;
  2. Where he or she was unable to appear at an employment security office due to a job interview, etc. with a prospective employer arranged through job placement by an employment security office;
  3. Where he or she was unable to appear at an employment security office in order to receive vocational skills development training, etc. as directed by the head of an employment security office;
  4. Where he or she was unable to appear at an employment security office due to a natural disaster or any other unavoidable reason.
  (4) When recognizing unemployment under paragraph (1), the head of an employment security office shall take measures prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as supporting the formulation of plans for reemployment activities and job placement, to promote the reemployment of eligible recipients. In such cases, eligible recipients shall comply with the measures taken by the head of the employment security office unless there is good cause.

Article 45 (Daily wage serving as the basis for benefits) (1) The daily wage that serves as the basis for calculating job-seeking benefits (hereinafter referred to as the "basic daily wage") shall be the average wage calculated under Article 2(1)6 of the Labor Standards Act at the time of the most recent separation from employment related to recognition of eligibility for benefits under Article 43(1); provided, if the employee acquired insured status at least 2 times within 3 months before the date of the most recent separation from employment, the basic daily wage shall be the amount obtained by dividing the total amount of wages paid to the employee during the 3 months before the date of the most recent separation from employment (for daily employees, during the 4 months before the date of the most recent separation from employment, excluding the last 1 month) by the total number of days in the 3-month period that serves as the basis for calculation.
  (2) If the amount calculated under paragraph (1) is less than the ordinary wage of the employee under the Labor Standards Act, the amount of such ordinary wage shall be the basic daily wage; provided, this shall not apply to a person who was a daily employee at the time of separation from employment in the most recent business. <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (3) If it is difficult to calculate the basic daily wage under paragraphs (1) and (2) or if insurance premiums have been paid based on the standard remuneration under Article 3 of the Insurance Premium Collection Act (hereinafter referred to as "standard remuneration"), the standard remuneration shall be the basic daily wage; provided, even where insurance premiums have been paid based on the standard remuneration, this shall not apply if the basic daily wage calculated under paragraphs (1) and (2) exceeds the standard remuneration. <Amended on Jan. 27, 2010; Jan. 5, 2021>
  (4) Notwithstanding paragraphs (1) through (3), if the basic daily wage calculated under those provisions is less than the amount obtained by multiplying the prescribed working hours per day before separation from employment by the hourly minimum wage applicable at the time of separation from employment under the Minimum Wage Act (hereinafter referred to as the "minimum basic daily wage"), the minimum basic daily wage shall be the basic daily wage. In such cases, the prescribed working hours per day before separation from employment shall be calculated in the manner prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jan. 20, 2015>
  (5) Notwithstanding paragraphs (1) through (3), if the basic daily wage calculated under those provisions exceeds the amount prescribed by Presidential Decree, taking into account the purpose of the insurance and the wage level of ordinary employees, the amount prescribed by Presidential Decree shall be the basic daily wage.

Article 46 (Daily amount of job-seeking benefits) (1) The daily amount of job-seeking benefits shall be as follows: <Amended on Aug. 27, 2019>
  1. In cases under Article 45(1) through (3) and (5), an amount equal to 60/100 of the eligible recipient's basic daily wage;
  2. In cases under Article 45(4), an amount equal to 80/100 of the eligible recipient's basic daily wage (hereinafter referred to as "minimum daily amount of job-seeking benefits").
  (2) If the daily amount of job-seeking benefits calculated under paragraph (1)1 is less than the minimum daily amount of job-seeking benefits, the minimum daily amount of job-seeking benefits shall be the daily amount of job-seeking benefits of the eligible recipient.

Article 47 (Reporting on employment during the period subject to recognition of unemployment) (1) If an eligible recipient obtains employment satisfying the criteria prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor during the period for which he or she seeks recognition of unemployment (hereinafter referred to as the "period subject to recognition of unemployment"), he or she shall report such fact to the head of an employment security office. <Amended on Jul. 21, 2011; Jan. 15, 2019>
  (2) If deemed necessary, the head of an employment security office may investigate whether an eligible recipient obtained employment during the period subject to recognition of unemployment. <Amended on Jul. 21, 2011; Jan. 15, 2019>
  [Title Amended on Jul. 21, 2011; Jan. 15, 2019]

Article 48 (Benefit period and number of benefit days) (1) Except as otherwise provided in this Act, job-seeking benefits shall be paid, beginning on the day following the date of separation from employment related to eligibility for such job-seeking benefits, and within 12 months, for up to the specified number of benefit days under Article 50(1).
  (2) If a person who is unable to obtain employment during the 12-month period under paragraph (1) due to pregnancy, childbirth, child care, or any other reason prescribed by Presidential Decree reports such fact to an employment security office within the benefit period, job-seeking benefits shall be paid, for up to the specified number of benefit days under Article 50(1), during the period obtained by adding the period during which he or she is unable to obtain employment to the 12-month period (if the period exceeds 4 years, it shall be 4 years). <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (3) In any of the following cases, the report under paragraph (2) shall be deemed to have been filed on the relevant first day of medical care: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2008; May 26, 2020>
  1. Where medical care benefits under Article 40 of the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act are paid;
  2. Where a person who separated from employment because he or she needed medical care for at least 3 months due to a disease or injury, and the fact that he or she had difficulty engaging in job-seeking activities during the period of separation from employment has been verified through the opinion of the attending physician specifically stating the period of medical care and the status of the injury or disease and the opinion of the business owner stating that the person separated from employment for medical care.

Article 49 (Waiting period) (1) Notwithstanding Article 44, job-seeking benefits shall not be paid during the 7-day period beginning on the date of reporting unemployment under Article 42, which shall be regarded as a waiting period; provided, in the case of a person who was a daily employee in the construction industry at the time of the most recent separation from employment, job-seeking benefits shall be paid beginning on the date of reporting unemployment under Article 42. <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019; Dec. 31, 2022>
  (2) Notwithstanding the main clause of paragraph (1), if an application for recognition of eligibility for benefits has been filed under Article 43(1) or 43-2(1), and the reason for separation from employment related to the insured status most recently lost falls under the proviso of Article 43-2(2), the period prescribed by Presidential Decree, not exceeding 4 weeks, beginning on the date of reporting unemployment under Article 42, shall be regarded as the waiting period, and no job-seeking benefits shall not be paid during that period. <Added on Dec. 31, 2022>

Article 50 (Specified number of benefit days and period of covered employment) (1) The number of days for which job-seeking benefits are payable based on a single eligibility for benefits (hereinafter referred to as the "specified number of benefit days") shall be the period beginning on the day following the end of the waiting period and ending on the day on which the number of days specified in Appendix 1 according to the period of covered employment and age is reached. <Amended on Jul. 21, 2011>
  (2) If an eligible recipient extends the benefit period under Article 48(2) within the specified number of benefit days due to pregnancy, childbirth, child care, or any other reason prescribed by Presidential Decree, payment of job-seeking benefits shall be deferred for the period of such extension.
  (3) The period of covered employment shall be the period during which the person was employed in a covered business at the time of separation from employment related to the eligibility for benefits (excluding any period during which the person was employed as an employee excluded from application under Articles 10 and 10-2; hereafter in this Article the same shall apply); provided, in the case of an insured self-employed person, the period of covered employment shall be the period for which employment insurance premiums were actually paid during the insurance coverage period for the covered business at the time of permanent closure of the business related to the eligibility for benefits. <Amended on Jul. 21, 2011; Jan. 15, 2019>
  (4) Notwithstanding paragraph (3), in any of the following cases, the period of covered employment shall be calculated as follows: <Amended on Jul. 21, 2011>
  1. If a person lost insured status in a previous covered business and acquires insured status in the current covered business within 3 years from the date of such loss: The period of covered employment in the previous covered business shall be aggregated; provided, if the person has received job-seeking benefits due to the loss of insured status in the previous covered business, the period of covered employment in that previous covered business shall be excluded;
  2. If an insured self-employed person was previously employed as an employee, lost insured status, and reacquires insured status as a self-employed person within 3 years from the date of such loss: The period of covered employment in the previous covered business shall not be aggregated, but shall be aggregated only if the insured self-employed person requests that the previous period of covered employment be aggregated; provided, if the person has received job-seeking benefits due to the loss of insured status in the previous covered business, the period of covered employment in that previous covered business shall be excluded.
  (5) With respect to an insured person whose acquisition of insured status was not reported, if the date on which he or she became insured during a single period of covered employment falls before January 1 of the year that is 3 years before the relevant date specified in any of the following subparagraphs, the period of covered employment shall be calculated, notwithstanding paragraph (3), deeming that he or she acquired insured status on the first day of the insurance year in which the date 3 years before the relevant date falls; provided, if it is proved that the business owner continuously paid employment insurance premiums for the insured person from a date before January 1 of the year that is 3 years before the relevant date specified in any of the following subparagraphs, the period of covered employment shall be calculated based on the period for which employment insurance premiums were paid: <Amended on Jan. 20, 2015>
  1. The date on which acquisition of insured status was reported under Article 15;
  2. The date on which acquisition of insured status was verified under Article 17.
  [Title Amended on Jul. 21, 2011]

Article 51 (Extended training benefits) (1) The head of an employment security office may direct an eligible recipient to receive vocational skills development training, etc., if such training is necessary for his or her reemployment in consideration of the eligible recipient's age, career experience, and other factors.
  (2) If the head of an employment security office has directed an eligible recipient to receive vocational skills development training, etc. under paragraph (1), he or she may extend payment of job-seeking benefits beyond the specified number of benefit days with respect to days during the period in which the eligible recipient receives such training, etc. for which recognition of unemployment has been obtained. In such cases, the period during which such extended job-seeking benefits (hereinafter referred to as “extended training benefits”) are payable shall not exceed the period prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) Trainees and training courses under paragraph (1), and other necessary matters, shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 52 (Individual extended benefits) (1) The head of an employment security office may extend payment of job-seeking benefits beyond the specified number of benefit days to an eligible recipient prescribed by Presidential Decree who has particular difficulty in obtaining employment and is in financial hardship, with respect to days for which he or she has obtained recognition of unemployment. <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (2) Job-seeking benefits extended under paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as “individual extended benefits”) shall be paid for a period prescribed by Presidential Decree not exceeding 60 days.

Article 53 (Special extended benefits) (1) If a reason prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as a rapid increase in unemployment, occurs, the Minister of Employment and Labor may extend payment of job-seeking benefits beyond the specified number of benefit days for up to 60 days with respect to days for which eligible recipients have obtained recognition of unemployment; provided, this shall not apply to eligible recipients prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor, including those who have income at or above a certain level for maintaining financial stability after separation from employment. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (2) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall implement the payment of job-seeking benefits extended under the main clause of paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as "special extended benefits") for a specified period. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 54 (Extended benefit period and daily amount of job-seeking benefits) (1) If extended benefits under Articles 51 through 53 are paid, the benefit period of the relevant eligible recipient shall be the period calculated by adding the number of days for which job-seeking benefits are extended to the benefit period of that eligible recipient under Article 48.
  (2) If extended training benefits are paid under Article 51, the daily amount thereof shall be 100/100 of the daily amount of job-seeking benefits of the relevant eligible recipient, and if individual extended benefits or special extended benefits are paid under Article 52 or 53, the daily amount thereof shall be 70/100 of the daily amount of job-seeking benefits of the relevant eligible recipient. <Amended on Mar. 21, 2008>
  (3) If the daily amount of job-seeking benefits calculated under paragraph (2) is less than the minimum daily amount of job-seeking benefits under Article 46(2), the eligible recipient shall receive the minimum daily amount of job-seeking benefits.

Article 55 (Coordination of extended benefits) (1) Extended benefits under Articles 51 through 53 shall be paid after all job-seeking benefits payable to the eligible recipient under Article 48 have been paid.
  (2) Individual extended benefits and special extended benefits shall not be paid to an eligible recipient receiving extended training benefits until all such extended training benefits have been paid.
  (3) If an eligible recipient receiving individual extended benefits or special extended benefits comes to receive extended training benefits, individual extended benefits or special extended benefits shall no longer be paid.
  (4) Individual extended benefits shall not be paid to an eligible recipient receiving special extended benefits until all such special extended benefits have been paid, and special extended benefits shall not be paid to an eligible recipient receiving individual extended benefits until all such individual extended benefits have been paid.
  (5) Other matters necessary for coordinating extended benefits shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 55-2 (Support for National Pension contributions) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor may provide support for part of the National Pension contributions to an eligible recipient who intends to have the period during which he or she receives job-seeking benefits additionally included in his or her period of coverage under Article 19-2(1) of the National Pension Act.
  (2) The amount of support under paragraph (1) shall exceed 25/100 of the pension contributions under Article 19-2(3) of the National Pension Act.
  (3) Matters necessary for the procedures and methods of support under paragraph (1), the amount of support under paragraph (2), etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on May 29, 2016]

Article 56 (Payment dates and methods of payment) (1) Job-seeking benefits shall be paid for the number of days for which recognition of unemployment has been obtained, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) The head of an employment security office shall determine the payment date for job-seeking benefits for each eligible recipient and notify him or her thereof.

Article 57 (Unpaid job-seeking benefits) (1) If an eligible recipient dies and any job-seeking benefits payable to him or her remain unpaid, such unpaid benefits shall be paid, upon claim, to the spouse (including a person in a de facto marital relationship), child, parent, grandchild, grandparent, or sibling of the eligible recipient who shared a livelihood with him or her. <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (2) With respect to a period during which the eligible recipient was unable to obtain recognition of unemployment due to his or her death, a person claiming payment unpaid job-seeking benefits under paragraph (1) shall obtain recognition of unemployment for the eligible recipient, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, if the eligible recipient falls under Article 47(1), the person claiming unpaid job-seeking benefits shall report to the head of an employment security office under that paragraph. <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (3) The order of priority among persons eligible to receive unpaid job-seeking benefits under paragraph (1) shall be the order listed in that paragraph. In such cases, if there are 2 or more persons in the same priority, a claim filed by 1 of them shall be deemed to have been filed on behalf of all of them, and payment made to that person shall be deemed payment to all of them. <Amended on May 26, 2020>

Article 58 (Restriction on eligibility for benefits based on reasons for separation from employment) Notwithstanding Article 40, if the head of an employment security office recognizes that an insured person falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the insured person shall be deemed ineligible for benefits: <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010; May 26, 2020>
  1. An insured person who has been dismissed for any of the following serious causes attributable to him or her:
  a. Where the person has been sentenced to imprisonment without labor or a heavier punishment for violating the Criminal Act or any statute related to his or her duties;
  b. Where the person has caused serious disruption to business operations or substantial property damage and meets the criteria prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor;
  c. Where the person has been absent from work without authorization for a prolonged period without good cause in violation of the employment contract, rules of employment, etc.;
  2. An insured person who separated from employment due to his or her own circumstances and falls under any of the following:
  a. Where the person separated from employment in order to take another job or engage in self-employment;
  b. Where the person, despite having a serious cause attributable to him or her under subparagraph 1, separated from employment upon the recommendation of the business owner instead of being dismissed;
  c. Where the person separated from employment for a reason other than good cause prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor.

Article 59 Deleted. <Jan. 20, 2015>

Article 60 (Suspension of benefits for refusal of training) (1) If an eligible recipient refuses to accept a job referred by the head of an employment security office or refuses to receive vocational skills development training, etc. directed by the head of an employment security office, payment of job-seeking benefits shall be suspended, as prescribed by Presidential Decree; provided, this shall not apply if there is good cause falling under any of the following subparagraphs: <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  1. Where the job referred or the occupational category for which the eligible recipient has been directed to participate in vocational skills development training, etc. is not suited to the abilities of the eligible recipient;
  2. Where relocation of the recipient’s residence is necessary in order to accept a job or participate in vocational skills development training, etc., but such relocation is impracticable;
  3. Where the wage level of the job referred is at least 20/100 lower than the ordinary wage level for the same type of work or the same level of skill in the same region, or where the job falls under the criteria determined by the Minister of Employment and Labor;
  4. Where there is any other good cause.
  (2) If an eligible recipient refuses, without good cause, vocational guidance for facilitating reemployment conducted by the head of an employment security office in accordance with the criteria determined by the Minister of Employment and Labor, payment of job-seeking benefits shall be suspended, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (3) Whether good cause exists for purposes of the proviso of paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be determined by the head of an employment security office in accordance with the criteria determined by the Minister of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (4) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall determine and publicly notify the period of suspension of job-seeking benefits, under paragraphs (1) and (2), which shall not exceed 1 month. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 61 (Restriction on payment of benefits due to improper acts) (1) No job-seeking benefits shall be paid to a person who has received or attempted to receive unemployment benefits by fraud or other improper means, from the date on which the person received or attempted to receive such benefits; provided, if the person newly acquires eligibility for benefits after the separation from employment related to such benefits, this shall not apply to job-seeking benefits payable under such newly acquired eligibility for benefits. <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (2) Notwithstanding the main clause of paragraph (1), if the fraud or other improper means falls under grounds prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as failure to comply with the reporting obligation under Article 47(1) or filing a false report, no job-seeking benefits shall be paid for the relevant period subject to recognition of unemployment only; provided, if such violations are committed on 2 or more occasions, the main clause of paragraph (1) shall apply. <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (3) If a person who has received or attempted to receive unemployment benefits by fraud or other improper means becomes ineligible to receive job-seeking benefits under paragraph (1) or (2), such person shall be deemed to have received such job-seeking benefits for purposes of applying Article 50(3) and (4). <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (4) If a person who has received or attempted to receive unemployment benefits by fraud or other improper means becomes ineligible to receive job-seeking benefits under paragraph (1) or (2), such person shall be deemed to have received job-seeking benefits for the number of days for which payment of job-seeking benefits has been denied, for purposes of applying Article 63(2). <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (5) Notwithstanding the proviso of paragraph (1), if a person who has received or attempted to receive job-seeking benefits by fraud or other improper means has been denied job-seeking benefits under the main clause of paragraph (1) on 3 or more occasions during the 10 years preceding the date on which the person received such job-seeking benefits or filed a report on recognition of unemployment under Article 44, no job-seeking benefits payable under such newly acquired eligibility for benefits shall be paid for a period not exceeding 3 years, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, from the date on which the person received such job-seeking benefits by fraud or other improper means or filed a report on recognition of unemployment under Article 44. <Added on Aug. 27, 2019>

Article 62 (Order for return) (1) The head of an employment security office may order a person who has received job-seeking benefits by fraud or other improper means to return all or part of the job-seeking benefits received, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor.
  (2) If the head of an employment security office orders a person to return job-seeking benefits under paragraph (1), he or she may, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor, collect an additional amount not exceeding twice the amount of job-seeking benefits received by fraud or other improper means; provided, where the person has received job-seeking benefits by fraud or other improper means by conspiring (referring to cases in which the fraud or other improper means includes a reason attributable to the business owner, such as a false declaration, report, or certification by the business owner; hereinafter the same shall apply) with the business owner (including a representative or employee of the business owner and any other person acting on behalf of the business owner; hereafter in this Article and Article 116(1) the same shall apply), he or she may collect an additional amount not exceeding 5 times the amount of the job-seeking benefits so received.
  (3) If a person who has received job-seeking benefits by fraud or other improper means has conspired with the business owner, the business owner shall be jointly and severally liable with that person for the return of the job-seeking benefits and payment of any additional amount under paragraphs (1) and (2).
  (4) If job-seeking benefits have been erroneously paid to a person who is or was eligible for job-seeking benefits, the head of an employment security office may order the return of the amount so paid.
  (5) If a person who is required to return the amount of job-seeking benefits paid or pay an additional amount under paragraph (1),(2), or (4) is entitled to receive job-seeking benefits under this Act, the head of an employment security office may, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, apply such job-seeking benefits to the amount to be returned or the additional amount under paragraph (1),(2), or (4).
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Aug. 27, 2019]

Article 63 (Special cases concerning sickness benefits) (1) Notwithstanding Article 44(1), with respect to any days for which an eligible recipient is unable to obtain recognition of unemployment because he or she is unable to work due to illness, injury, or childbirth after reporting unemployment under Article 42, an amount equivalent to the daily amount of job-seeking benefits under Article 46 (hereinafter referred to as “sickness benefits”) may, upon the request of the eligible recipient, be paid in lieu of job-seeking benefits; provided, no sickness benefits shall be paid for any period during which payment of job-seeking benefits is suspended under Article 60(1) and (2). <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (2) The number of days for which sickness benefits may be paid shall not exceed the number obtained by subtracting the number of days for which job-seeking benefits have been paid under the relevant eligibility for benefits from the specified number of benefit days applicable to that eligibility for benefits.
