In such cases, when applying the provisions of this Act (excluding Articles 61 and 62) to a person who has received sickness benefits, job-seeking benefits corresponding to the number of days for which sickness benefits have been paid shall be deemed to have been paid. <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (3) Sickness benefits under paragraph (1) shall be paid on the first date on which job-seeking benefits are paid after the reason preventing employment has ceased to exist (or, if there is no such date, on a date determined by the head of an employment security office); provided, if deemed necessary, sickness benefits may be paid as separately determined by the Minister of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (4) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), no sickness benefits shall be paid to an eligible recipient who is entitled to receive compensation for suspension of work under Article 79 of the Labor Standards Act, temporary disability benefits under Articles 52 through 56 of the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act, or any other compensation or benefits prescribed by Presidential Decree as corresponding thereto. <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019>
  (5) Articles 47,49,57,61 (excluding paragraph (4)), and 62 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the payment of sickness benefits. In such cases, "period subject to recognition of unemployment" shall be construed as "days for which recognition of unemployment has not been obtained", and "job-seeking benefits" shall be construed as "sickness benefits". <Amended on Aug. 27, 2019>

SECTION 3 Employment Promotion Allowances

Article 64 (Early re-employment allowances) (1) Early re-employment allowances shall be paid to an eligible recipient (excluding a foreign employee defined in Article 2 of the Act on the Employment of Foreign Workers) who obtains stable reemployment or engages in a for-profit business on his or her own account, where the recipient falls under the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), no early re-employment allowances shall be paid to an eligible recipient who has received early re-employment allowances within the period prescribed by Presidential Decree before the date on which he or she obtained stable reemployment or commenced a for-profit business on his or her own account.
  (3) The amount of early re-employment allowances shall be the amount calculated in accordance with the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree based on the ratio of unpaid benefit days to the specified number of benefit days for job-seeking benefits.
  (4) When applying the provisions of this Act (excluding Articles 61 and 62) to a person who has received early re-employment allowances, job-seeking benefits for the number of days obtained by dividing the amount of the early re-employment allowances by the daily amount of job-seeking benefits under Article 46 shall be deemed to have been paid to that person. <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (5) An incentive may be paid, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to a person who has helped an eligible recipient obtain early reemployment, thereby shortening the payment period of job-seeking benefits. <Amended on May 26, 2020>

Article 65 (Vocational skill development allowances) (1) Vocational skills development allowances shall be paid to an eligible recipient who receives vocational skills development training, etc. directed by the head of an employment security office, for the period during which he or she receives such training, etc.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), vocational skills development allowances shall not be paid for any period during which payment of job-seeking benefits is suspended under Article 60(1) and (2).
  (3) Matters necessary for the requirements for and amount of vocational skills development allowances shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, a different amount of vocational skills development allowances may be prescribed for vocational skills development training, etc. relating to occupations publicly notified by the Minister of Employment and Labor as particularly necessary in consideration of the supply of and demand for human resources. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 66 (Long-distance job search allowances) (1) Long-distance job search allowances may be paid if an eligible recipient conducts job-seeking activities over a wide area pursuant to a referral by an employment security office and the head of the employment security office deems it necessary in accordance with the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) The amount of long-distance job search allowances shall be based on the ordinary expenses incurred in conducting the job-seeking activities under paragraph (1), and shall be calculated as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 67 (Relocation allowances) (1) Relocation allowances may be paid if an eligible recipient relocates his or her residence in order to obtain employment or receive vocational skills development training, etc. directed by the head of an employment security office and the head of the employment security office deems it necessary in accordance with the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) The amount of relocation allowances shall be based on the ordinary expenses incurred in relocating an eligible recipient and his or her cohabiting relatives who depend on the eligible recipient for their livelihood, and shall be calculated as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 68 (Restriction on payment of employment promotion allowances) (1) No employment promotion allowances shall be paid to a person who has received or attempted to receive unemployment benefits by fraud or other improper means from the date on which he or she received or attempted to receive such benefits; provided, if the person acquires new eligibility for benefits after separating from employment related to such benefits, this shall not apply to employment promotion allowances payable under such new eligibility for benefits. <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (2) Notwithstanding the main clause of paragraph (1), if the fraud or other improper means falls under any of the grounds prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as failure to comply with the reporting obligation under Article 47(1) or filing a false report, payment of employment promotion allowances shall not be restricted; provided, where the person commits violations on 2 or more occasions, the main clause of paragraph (1) shall apply.
  (3) If a person who has received or attempted to receive unemployment benefits by fraud or other improper means becomes unable to receive employment promotion allowances under paragraph (1) or (2) and consequently, is unable to receive early re-employment allowances, the person shall be deemed to have received the early re-employment allowances that he or she is unable to receive when applying Article 64(4). <Amended on May 26, 2020>

Article 69 (Application mutatis mutandis) Articles 57(1) and (3) and 62 shall apply mutatis mutandis to employment promotion allowances. In such cases, "eligible recipient" shall be construed as "a person entitled to receive employment promotion allowances", and "job-seeking benefits" shall be construed as "employment promotion allowances". <Amended on Aug. 27, 2019; May 26, 2020>

SECTION 4 Special Cases concerning Application of Unemployment Benefits for Insured Self-Employed Persons

Article 69-2 (Types of unemployment benefits for insured self-employed persons) Types of unemployment benefits for insured self-employed persons shall be those under Article 37; provided, extended benefits under Articles 51 through 55 and early re-employment allowances under Article 64 shall not apply.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 21, 2011]

Article 69-3 (Eligibility requirements for job-seeking benefits) Job-seeking benefits shall be paid if an insured self-employed person who has discontinued business satisfies all of the following requirements: <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  1. The qualifying days in covered employment as an insured self-employed person under the proviso of Article 41(1) shall total at least 1 year during the 24-month period before the date of discontinuance of business;
  2. The person shall be in a state of being unable to obtain employment despite being willing and able to work;
  3. The reason for discontinuance of business shall not fall under any ground for restriction on eligibility for benefits under Article 69-7;
  4. The person shall actively seek re-employment.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 21, 2011]

Article 69-4 (Basic daily wage) (1) The basic daily wage applicable to an eligible recipient who was an insured self-employed person shall be the amount obtained by adding up all amounts of remuneration publicly notified under Article 49-2(3) of the Insurance Premium Collection Act, which serve as the basis for calculating the insurance premiums paid by the person during the period specified in the relevant subparagraph, and dividing the total by the total number of days in that period: <Amended on Jan. 15, 2021>
  1. Where the period of covered employment related to eligibility for benefits is at least 3 years: The period of covered employment of 3 years before the last date of discontinuance of business;
  2. Where the period of covered employment related to eligibility for benefits is less than 3 years: The period of covered employment related to eligibility for benefits.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where the specified number of benefit days under Article 69-6 additionally increases as a result of aggregating periods of covered employment under Article 50(4) for an eligible recipient who was an insured self-employed person, the basic daily wage for the increased number of days shall be the basic daily wage calculated under paragraph (1); provided, if such basic daily wage falls under the following subparagraphs, the amount specified in the relevant subparagraph shall apply:
  1. Where the basic daily wage is less than the minimum basic daily wage: The minimum basic daily wage;
  2. Where the basic daily wage exceeds the amount prescribed by Presidential Decree under Article 45(5): The amount prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 21, 2011]

Article 69-5 (Daily amount of job-seeking benefits) The daily amount of job-seeking benefits for an eligible recipient who was an insured self-employed person and has discontinued business shall be 60/100 of the eligible recipient's basic daily wage. <Amended on Aug. 27, 2019>
  [This Article Added on Jul. 21, 2011]

Article 69-6 (Specified number of benefit days) The specified number of benefit days for an eligible recipient who was an insured self-employed person and has discontinued business shall the period beginning on the day following the end of the waiting period under Article 49 and ending when the number of days specified in Appendix 2 according to the period of covered employment has elapsed.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 21, 2011]

Article 69-7 (Restriction on eligibility for benefits based on reasons for discontinuance of business) Notwithstanding Article 69-3, where the head of an employment security office determines that an insured self-employed person who has discontinued business falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the person shall be deemed ineligible for benefits:
  1. Where the person has discontinued business as a result of revocation of a permit or suspension of business operations for violation of statutes or regulations;
  2. Where the person has discontinued business due to any ground prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor that constitutes gross misconduct on his or her part, such as arson;
  3. Where the person has discontinued business in order to obtain employment or to start another self-employed business for any ground other than those prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor, such as a sharp decline in sales;
  4. Where the person has discontinued business for any ground that does not constitute good cause prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 21, 2011]

Article 69-8 (Restriction on payment of unemployment benefits to insured self-employed persons) The Minister of Employment and Labor may withhold payment of unemployment benefits under this Chapter to a person who is in arrears with insurance premiums, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 21, 2011]

Article 69-9 (Application mutatis mutandis) (1) Articles 37-2, 38, 38-2, 42, 43, 43-2, 44, 47 through 49, 56, 57, 60 through 63, and 65 through 68 shall apply mutatis mutandis to unemployment benefits for insured self-employed persons. In such cases, "separation from employment" in Articles 42(1) and 43(3) shall be construed as "discontinuance of business"; "Article 40(1)1 through 3,5, and 6" in Article 43(1) shall be construed as "Article 69-3"; "Article 46" in Article 63(1) shall be construed as "Article 69-5"; and "Article 50(1)" in Article 48(1) shall be construed as "Article 69-6". <Amended on Jun. 4, 2013; Jan. 5, 2021; Dec. 31, 2 022>>
  (2) Articles 57(1) and (3) and 62 shall apply mutatis mutandis to employment promotion allowances (excluding early re-employment allowances) for insured self-employed persons. In such cases, "eligible recipient" in Article 57(1) shall be construed as "a person entitled to receive employment promotion allowances". <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  [This Article Added on Jul. 21, 2011]

CHAPTER V CHILD CARE LEAVE BENEFITS

SECTION 1 Child Care Leave Benefits and Benefits for Reduced Working Hours during Periods of Child Care

Article 70 (Child care leave benefits) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall pay child care leave benefits to an insured employee who has been granted child care leave under Article 19 of the Equal Employment Opportunity and Work-Family Balance Assistance Act for at least 30 days (excluding any period overlapping with maternity leave under Article 74 of the Labor Standards Act) and whose qualifying days in covered employment under Article 41 total at least 180 days before the date the child care leave begins: <Amended on Dec. 21, 2007; Jun. 4, 2010; Jul. 21, 2011; Feb. 1, 2012; Jan. 21, 2014; Aug. 27, 2019; May 26, 2020>
  1. Deleted; <Aug. 27, 2019>
  2. Deleted; <Aug. 27, 2019>
  3. Deleted. <Jul. 21, 2011>
  (2) A person who intends to receive child care leave benefits under paragraph (1) shall apply therefor from 1 month after the date on which the child care leave begins until 12 months after the date on which the child care leave ends; provided, a person who was unable to apply for child care leave benefits during that period due to any reason prescribed by Presidential Decree shall apply therefor within 30 days after the reason ceases to exist. <Added on Jul. 21, 2011>
  (3) Where an insured person applies for child care leave benefits under paragraph (2), if they have separated from employment during the period of child care leave or obtained employment falling under the criteria prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor, he or she shall state such fact in the application. <Added on Jan. 15, 2019>
  (4) The amount of child care leave benefits under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jul. 21, 2011; Jan. 15, 2019>
  (5) Matters necessary for the application for, and payment of, child care leave benefits shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010; Jul. 21, 2011; Jan. 15, 2019>

Article 71 (Verification of child care leave) If an insured person applies for child care leave benefits under Article 70, the business owner shall actively cooperate in the verification of relevant facts and all related procedures, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 72 Deleted. <Jan. 15, 2019>

Article 73 (Restriction on payment of child care leave benefits) (1) If an insured person separates from employment during the period of child care leave, no child care leave benefits shall be paid to him or her from the date of such separation from employment. <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019>
  (2) If an insured person obtains employment meeting the criteria under Article 70(3) during the period of child care leave, no child care leave benefits shall be paid for the period of such employment. <Added on Jan. 15, 2019>
  (3) If an insured person receives money or other valuables from the business owner due to child care leave, child care leave benefits may be reduced, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019>
  (4) No child care leave benefits shall be paid to a person who has received or attempted to receive child care leave benefits by fraud or other improper means from the date on which the person received or attempted to receive such benefits; provided, this shall not apply where the person meets the requirements for child care leave benefits anew after the child care leave related to such benefits. <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019>
  (5) Notwithstanding the main clause of paragraph (4), if a person has received or attempted to receive child care leave benefits by failing to state, or falsely stating, the fact that he or she obtained employment during the period of child care leave in violation of Article 70(3), the scope of child care leave benefits subject to restriction on payment may be determined differently as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor, taking into consideration the number of violations, etc. <Added on Jan. 15, 2019>
  [Title Amended on Jan. 15, 2019]

Article 73-2 (Benefits for reduced working hours during periods of child care) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall pay benefits for reduced working hours during periods of child care to an insured person who has taken reduced working hours during periods of child care under Article 19-2 of the Equal Employment Opportunity and Work-Family Balance Assistance Act (hereinafter referred to as "reduced working hours during periods of child care") for at least 30 days (excluding any period overlapping with maternity leave under Article 74 of the Labor Standards Act) and whose qualifying days in covered employment under Article 41 before the date on which reduced working hours during periods of child care begin total at least 180 days: <Amended on Feb. 1, 2012; Jan. 21, 2014; Aug. 27, 2019; May 26, 2020>
  1. Deleted; <Aug. 27, 2019>
  2. Deleted. <Aug. 27, 2019>
  (2) A person who intends to receive benefits for reduced working hours during periods of child care under paragraph (1) shall apply for such benefits not earlier than 1 month after the date on which the reduced working hours during periods of child care begin and within 12 months after the date on which they end; provided, a person who was unable to apply for such benefits during that period due to any reason prescribed by Presidential Decree shall apply for such benefits within 30 days after such reason ceases to exist.
  (3) The amount of benefits for reduced working hours during periods of child care under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (4) Matters necessary for the application for, and payment of, benefits for reduced working hours during periods of child care shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 21, 2011]

Article 74 (Application mutatis mutandis) (1) Article 62 shall apply mutatis mutandis to child care leave benefits. In such cases, "job-seeking benefits" shall be construed as "child care leave benefits". <Amended on Jul. 21, 2011>
  (2) Articles 62,71, and 73 shall apply mutatis mutandis to benefits for reduced working hours during periods of child care. In such cases, "job-seeking benefits" in Article 62 shall be construed as "benefits for reduced working hours during periods of child care", and "child care leave" in Articles 71 and 73 shall be construed as "reduced working hours during periods of child care". <Added on Jul. 21, 2011; Jan. 5, 2021>

SECTION 2 Maternity Leave Benefits 등

Article 75 (Maternity leave benefits)) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall pay maternity leave benefits, etc. (hereinafter referred to as "maternity leave benefits, etc.") to an insured person who has taken maternity leave or miscarriage/stillbirth leave under Article 74 of the Labor Standards Act pursuant to Article 18 of the Equal Employment Opportunity and Work-Family Balance Assistance Act, or who has taken paternity leave under Article 18-2 of that Act or fertility treatment leave under Article 18-3 of that Act, and who satisfies all of the following requirements: <Amended on Dec. 21, 2007; Jun. 4, 2010; Feb. 1, 2012; Jan. 21, 2014; Aug. 27, 2019; May 26, 2020; Oct. 22, 2024>
  1. The insured person's qualifying days in covered employment under Article 41 before the date on which the leave ends shall total at least 180 days;
  2. The insured person shall apply for maternity leave benefits, etc. not earlier than 1 month after the date on which the leave begins [where the workplace of an insured person who has taken maternity leave or miscarriage/stillbirth leave is not an enterprise eligible for priority support, the date on which 60 days (75 days in the case of a woman pregnant with 2 or more children at the same time) have elapsed after the date on which the leave begins shall be deemed to be the date on which the leave begins] and within 12 months after the date on which the leave ends; provided, a person who was unable to apply for maternity leave benefits, etc. during that period due to any reason prescribed by Presidential Decree shall apply for maternity leave benefits, etc. within 30 days after such reason ceases to exist.
  [Title Amended on Feb. 1, 2012]

Article 75-2 (Subrogation of the right to receive maternity leave benefits, etc.) If a business owner has paid an employee, in advance, money or other valuables equivalent to maternity leave benefits, etc. for the same reason giving rise to maternity leave benefits, etc. and such payment is recognized as having been made in lieu of maternity leave benefits, etc., the business owner shall be subrogated to the employee's right to receive maternity leave benefits, etc. to the extent of the amount paid (not exceeding the limit under Article 76(2)). <Amended on Feb. 1, 2012>
  [This Article Added on Dec. 31, 2008]
  [Title Amended on Feb. 1, 2012]

Article 76 (Payment period) (1) Maternity leave benefits, etc. under Article 75 shall be paid in an amount equal to the ordinary wage under the Labor Standards Act (calculated based on the date on which the leave begins) for the following leave periods: <Amended on Feb. 1, 2012; Jan. 21, 2014; Aug. 27, 2019; Oct. 22, 2024>
  1. The period of maternity leave or miscarriage/stillbirth leave under Article 74 of the Labor Standards Act; provided, where the enterprise is not an enterprise eligible for priority support, the period shall be limited to the days exceeding 60 days (75 days in the case of a woman pregnant with 2 or more children at the same time) during such leave (up to a maximum of 30 days, 40 days where a premature infant is born, and 45 days in the case of a woman pregnant with 2 or more children at the same time);
  2. The period of paternity leave under Article 18-2 of the Equal Employment Opportunity and Work-Family Balance Assistance Act; provided, it shall be limited to cases where the workplace of the insured person is an enterprise eligible for priority support;
  3. The first 2 days of infertility treatment leave under Article 18-3 of the Equal Employment Opportunity and Work-Family Balance Assistance Act; provided, it shall be limited to cases where the workplace of the insured person is an enterprise eligible for priority support.
  (2) The minimum and maximum amounts of maternity leave benefits, etc. under paragraph (1) may be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Feb. 1, 2012>
  (3) Matters necessary for the application for, and payment of, maternity leave benefits, etc. under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010; Feb. 1, 2012>

Article 76-2 (Application to fixed-term employees or temporary agency workers) (1) Notwithstanding Article 76(1)1, where the term of the employment contract of a fixed-term employee defined in Article 2 of the Act on the Protection of Fixed-Term and Part-Time Employees or a temporary agency worker defined in Article 2 of the Act on the Protection of Temporary Agency Workers expires during the period of maternity leave or miscarriage/stillbirth leave under Article 74 of the Labor Standards Act, the Minister of Employment and Labor shall pay the fixed-term employee or temporary agency worker the full amount equivalent to maternity leave benefits, etc. for the period from the day following the date on which the employment contract expires to the date on which the maternity leave or miscarriage/stillbirth leave ends. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2022>
  (2) Matters necessary for the application for and payment of an amount equivalent to maternity leave benefits, etc., under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor.
  [This Article Added on Jan 5, 2021]

Article 77 (Application mutatis mutandis) (1) Articles 62,71, and 73 shall apply mutatis mutandis to orders for return, verification of facts, restrictions on payment, etc. relating to maternity leave benefits, etc. In such cases, "job-seeking benefits" in Article 62 shall be construed as "maternity leave benefits, etc.", and "child care leave" in Articles 71 and 73 shall be construed as "maternity leave, miscarriage/stillbirth leave, paternity leave, or fertility treatment leave". <Amended on Dec. 31, 2022; Oct. 22, 2024>
  (2) Articles 62,71, and 73 (excluding paragraph (1); hereafter in this paragraph, the same shall apply) shall apply mutatis mutandis to orders for return, verification of facts, restrictions on payment, etc. relating to amounts equivalent to maternity leave benefits, etc. under Article 76-2. In such cases, "job-seeking benefits" in Article 62 shall be construed as "amounts equivalent to maternity leave benefits, etc."; "child care leave" in Articles 71 and 73 shall be construed as "maternity leave or miscarriage/stillbirth leave"; and "child care leave benefits" in Articles 71 and 73 shall be construed as "amounts equivalent to maternity leave benefits, etc." <Added on Dec. 31, 2022>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 5, 2021]

CHAPTER V-2 SPECIAL CASES CONCERNING EMPLOYMENT INSURANCE FOR INSURED ARTISTS

Article 77-2 (Application to insured artists) (1) Under Article 8(2), this Chapter shall apply to an artist (hereinafter referred to as "artist"), meaning a person who is not an employee, who falls under persons prescribed by Presidential Decree, including artists defined in subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Artist Welfare Act, who enters into a contract related to culture and arts services under Article 4-4 of the Artist Welfare Act (hereinafter referred to as a "contract related to culture and arts services"), and who personally provides labor without employing another person, and to a business that enters into a contract related to culture and arts services with such person. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), this Act shall not apply where an artist falls under any of the following: <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021; Dec. 31, 2022>
  1. Where a person enters into an employment contract, a contract related to culture and arts services, or a contract for personal work under Article 77-6(1), or commences self-employment, after attaining the age of 65 (excluding cases where a person who maintained insured status before attaining the age of 65 continues under an employment contract, a contract related to culture and arts services, or a contract for personal work after attaining the age of 65);
  2. Where an artist fails to satisfy the income standards prescribed by Presidential Decree; provided, an artist whose contract term is less than 1 month (hereinafter referred to as a "short-term artist") shall be excluded;
  3. Where an artist is under the age of 15; provided, an artist under the age of 15 who wishes to be covered by employment insurance may enroll in employment insurance, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) Notwithstanding Article 15, where a project prescribed by Presidential Decree falls under any of the following subparagraphs, taking into consideration the characteristics, scale, and other relevant factors of the project, the project owner or the primary contractor shall file a report under Article 15 with respect to artists engaged by a subcontractor, as prescribed by Presidential Decree:
  1. Where multiple contracts are awarded for a single project, resulting in multiple primary contractors;
  2. Where a single project consists of multiple tiers of contracts, resulting in multiple subcontractors.
  (4) Where a project owner or a primary contractor requests relevant data, information, etc. prescribed by Presidential Decree for the purpose of filing a report on the acquisition, etc. of insured status, a business owner who is a subcontractor and the artist, etc. shall provide such data, information, etc.
  (5) Deleted. <Dec. 31, 2022>
  (6) The business owner of a business that has entered into a contract related to culture and arts services with an artist subject to this Chapter under paragraph (1) (referring to a project owner or a primary contractor in cases falling under paragraph (3)) shall bear insurance premiums under the Insurance Premium Collection Act, and the Insurance Premium Collection Act shall apply to matters necessary for the establishment, termination, and modification of the insurance relationship and for the calculation, payment, and collection of insurance premiums. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>
  [This Article Added on Jun. 9, 2020]

Article 77-3 (Job-seeking benefits for insured artists) (1) An artist shall be eligible for job-seeking benefits only when he or she satisfies all of the following requirements; provided, subparagraph 6 shall apply only to a person who was a short-term artist at the time of the most recent separation from employment: <Amended on Jan. 15, 2021>
  1. The artist shall have qualifying days in covered employment totaling at least 9 months during the 24-month period before the date of separation from employment;
  2. The artist shall be unemployed despite his or her willingness and ability to work or provide personal work (including engaging in a business for profit; hereafter in this Chapter the same shall apply);
  3. The reasons for the artist’s separation from employment shall not fall under any ground for restriction on eligibility for benefits under Article 58, as applied mutatis mutandis under Article 77-5(2); provided, notwithstanding subparagraph 2a of Article 58, as applied mutatis mutandis under Article 77-5(2), if the head of an employment security office determines that the artist was separated from employment due to a decrease in income as prescribed by Presidential Decree at the time of separation from employment, the separation from employment shall not be deemed to constitute a ground for restriction on eligibility for benefits under Article 58;
  4. The artist shall have maintained insured status as an insured artist for at least 3 months during the 24 months before the date of separation from employment;
  5. The artist shall actively endeavor to obtain reemployment;
  6. The artist shall satisfy all of the following requirements:
  a. The number of days on which the artist provided personal work during the 1 month before the date of application for recognition of eligibility for benefits shall be less than 10 days, or the artist shall not have provided personal work for 14 consecutive days before the date of application for recognition of eligibility for benefits;
  b. Where the artist has been separated from employment in another business due to a reason falling under a ground for restriction on eligibility for benefits under Article 58, as applied mutatis mutandis under Article 77-5(2), during the qualifying days in covered employment in the 24 months before the date of the most recent separation from employment, the artist shall have worked as a short-term artist for at least 90 days during those qualifying days in covered employment.
  (2) The qualifying days in covered employment under paragraph (1)1 shall be calculated from the date of acquisition of insured status in the business related to the eligibility for benefits to the date of separation from employment, and where a person has worked in at least 2 of the following during the 24 months before the date of separation from employment: an employee, an artist, and a personal work performer under Article 77-6(1), the qualifying days in covered employment shall be calculated as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>
  (3) The basic daily wage for an artist shall be the amount obtained by dividing the total remuneration reported under Article 16-10 of the Insurance Premium Collection Act during the 1-year period preceding the date of the last separation from employment related to the recognition of eligibility for benefits by the total number of days in the period serving as the basis for such calculation; provided, where the basic daily wage for an artist (excluding an artist who is not subject to standard remuneration under Article 3(1)2 of the Insurance Premium Collection Act) is less than the daily standard remuneration of an artist under Article 3 of that Act at the time of separation from employment, the daily standard remuneration shall be the basic daily wage. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021; Dec. 31, 2022>
  (4) The daily amount of job-seeking benefits for an artist shall be the amount obtained by multiplying the basic daily wage under paragraph (3) by 60/100.
  (5) The upper limit of the daily amount of job-seeking benefits under paragraph (4) shall be the amount prescribed by Presidential Decree, taking into consideration the upper limit of job-seeking benefits for insured employees and other relevant factors.
  (6) For an artist, the 7-day period beginning on the date of reporting unemployment under Article 42 shall be regarded as a waiting period, during which no job-seeking benefits shall be paid; provided, where any of the following reasons applies, a period prescribed by Presidential Decree for each such reason, not exceeding 4 weeks, shall be regarded as the waiting period, during which no job-seeking benefits shall be paid, and where 2 or more of the following reasons apply, the longest such period shall be regarded as the waiting period: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2022>
  1. Where the separation from employment is due to a reason specified in the proviso of paragraph (1)3;
  2. Where an application for recognition of eligibility for benefits has been filed under Article 43-2(1), and the reason for the separation from employment relating to the insured status most recently lost falls under the proviso of paragraph (2) of that Article.
  (7) The period of covered employment for calculating the specified number of days for which benefits are payable to an artist shall be the qualifying days in covered employment under paragraph (2); provided, in the case of a short-term artist, the period of covered employment shall be the period calculated as prescribed by Presidential Decree, taking into consideration the number of days on which personal work was provided, etc. during the relevant contract period.
  (8) Notwithstanding Article 47, where job-seeking benefits are paid to an insured artist, the head of an employment security office shall reduce the benefits in whole or in part and pay the reduced benefits, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, taking into consideration the level of income arising from employment, etc. during the period subject to recognition of unemployment and the duration of work or other activities.
  [This Article Added on Jun. 9, 2020]

Article 77-4 (Maternity benefits, etc. for artists) (1) Where an insured artist or a former insured artist is unable to provide personal work due to childbirth, miscarriage, or stillbirth, the Minister of Employment and Labor shall pay maternity benefits, etc. (hereinafter referred to as "maternity benefits, etc."); provided, where the requirements for payment of maternity leave benefits, etc. under Article 75 and maternity benefits, etc. under Article 77-9(1) are simultaneously satisfied with respect to the same child, or in any other case, such benefits shall be paid as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021; Jun. 10, 2022>
  (2) The eligibility requirements, benefit levels, payment periods, etc. for maternity benefits, etc. under paragraph (1) shall be as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) Matters necessary for the application for and payment of maternity benefits, etc. under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor.
  [This Article Added on Jun. 9, 2020]
  [Title Amended on Jun. 10, 2022]

Article 77-5 (Application mutatis mutandis) (1) Articles 13(1),14(1),15, and 17 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the insured status of an artist. In such cases, "employee" shall be construed as "artist"; "date of employment" as "date of commencement of a contract related to culture and arts services"; and "employee who was employed" as "artist whose contract related to culture and arts services has commenced". <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>
  (2) Articles 37-2,38,38-2,40(2)1,41(2),42,43,43-2,44,47,48,50,56 through 58, and 60 through 63 shall apply mutatis mutandis to job-seeking benefits for artists. In such cases, "during the 18 months before the date of separation from employment" in Article 40(2)1 shall be construed as "during the 24 months before the date of separation from employment", "Article 46" in the main clause of Article 63(1) as "Article 77-3(4) and (5)", and "Articles 47 and 49" in the former part of Article 63(5) as "Article 47". <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021; Dec. 31, 2022>
  (3) Articles 62 and 73(4) shall apply mutatis mutandis to orders for return, restrictions on payment, etc. relating to maternity benefits, etc. for artists. In such cases, "job-seeking benefits" in Article 62 shall be construed as "maternity benefits, etc."; "child care leave benefits" in Article 73(4) shall be construed as "maternity benefits, etc."; "child care leave" shall be construed as "childbirth, miscarriage, or stillbirth"; and "requirements for payment of child care leave benefits" shall be construed as "requirements for payment of maternity benefits, etc." <Amended on Dec. 31, 2022>
  (4) Articles 87 through 98, 99 (excluding paragraph (2)), and 100 through 112 shall apply mutatis mutandis to requests for verification of insured status and requests for review and further review relating to job-seeking benefits and maternity benefits, etc. for artists. In such cases, "unemployment benefits under Chapter IV and child care leave benefits and maternity leave benefits, etc. under Chapter V" and "unemployment benefits under Chapter IV and child care leave benefits and maternity leave benefits, etc. under Chapter V" shall each be construed as "job-seeking benefits and maternity benefits, etc. under Chapter V-2"; "unemployment benefits" each as "job-seeking benefits"; "workplace" each as "workplace and the office of a person required to report the acquisition of insured status"; "business owner" each as "business owner and a person required to report insured status"; "employee" each as "artist"; "child care leave benefits, etc." as "maternity benefits, etc."; "Chapter IV" as "Chapter V-2"; "child care leave benefits, benefits for reduced working hours during the period of child care, and maternity leave benefits, etc. under Chapter V" as "maternity benefits, etc. under Chapter V-2"; and "unemployment benefits, child care leave benefits, and maternity leave benefits, etc." as "job-seeking benefits and maternity benefits, etc." <Added on Dec. 31, 2022>
  [This Article Added on Jun. 9, 2020]

CHAPTER V-3 SPECIAL CASES CONCERNING EMPLOYMENT INSURANCE FOR INSURED PERSONAL WORK PERFORMERS

Article 77-6 (Application to insured personal work performers) (1) Pursuant to Article 8(2), this Chapter shall apply to a person, not an employee, from among persons who enter into a contract under which they provide personal work in person for the business of another person and receive consideration from the business owner or recipient of personal work (hereinafter referred to as a "contract for personal work"), who is engaged in an occupation prescribed by Presidential Decree (hereinafter referred to as a "personal work performer"), as well as to a business that enters into a contract for personal work with such person.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), this Act shall not apply where a personal work performer falls under any of the following: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2022>
  1. Where a personal work performer enters into an employment contract, a contract for personal work, or a contract related to culture and arts services after attaining the age of 65 (excluding cases where a person who maintained insured status before attaining the age of 65 continues to enter into such contracts after attaining the age of 65), or commences self-employment;
  2. Where a personal work performer fails to meet the income standards prescribed by Presidential Decree; provided, this subparagraph shall not apply to a personal work performer whose contract period is less than 1 month (hereinafter referred to as a "short-term personal work performer");
  3. Where a personal work performer is under the age of 15; provided, a personal work performer under the age of 15 who wishes to enroll in employment insurance may do so, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) Deleted. <Dec. 31, 2022>
  (4) A personal work performer to whom this Chapter applies pursuant to paragraph (1) and the business owner of a business that has entered into a contract for personal work with such person (hereinafter referred to as the "business owner of a personal work provision business") shall bear insurance premiums under the Insurance Premium Collection Act, and the Insurance Premium Collection Act shall apply to matters necessary for the establishment, termination, and modification of the insurance relationship and for the calculation, payment, and collection of insurance premiums.
  [This Article Added on Jan 5, 2021]

Article 77-7 (Special cases concerning personal work platform operators) (1) Notwithstanding Article 15, where the business owner of a personal work provision business enters into a contract for the use of a personal work platform (hereinafter referred to as a "contract for the use of a personal work platform") with a person who establishes and operates a system that collects and manages data and information relating to personal work performers and business owners of personal work provision businesses and records and processes such data and information in electronic form (hereinafter referred to as a "personal work platform"), that person (hereinafter referred to as a "personal work platform operator") shall file a report on the acquisition, etc. of insured status under Article 15(1) for the relevant personal work performer, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) The Minister of Employment and Labor may request a personal work platform operator to provide the following data or information necessary for verifying the use of the relevant personal work platform and the insurance relationship, in order to efficiently handle insurance affairs relating to personal work performers; in such cases, the personal work platform operator upon receipt of such request shall comply therewith unless there is good cause:
  1. The commencement date or termination date of the contract for the use of a personal work platform;
  2. Data or information prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the name and address of the workplace, relating to the insurance relationship of the business owner of a personal work provision business;
  3. Data or information prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the name, occupation, and remuneration of the personal work performer, relating to the insured status of the personal work performer.
  (3) If necessary to provide the data or information requested under paragraph (2), a personal work platform operator may request the relevant personal work performer and the business owner of a personal work provision business to provide necessary data or information. In such cases, the personal work performer and the business owner of a personal work provision business upon receipt of such request shall comply therewith unless there is good cause.
  (4) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall use data or information provided by a personal work platform operator under paragraph (2) only to the extent necessary for handling the relevant insurance affairs, and shall not disclose such data or information.
  (5) A personal work platform operator shall retain information relating to the reporting of insured status of a personal work performer under paragraph (1) on the personal work platform for 3 years from the date the contract for personal work concluded between the relevant personal work performer and the business owner of a personal work provision business ends.
  [This Article Added on Jan 5, 2021]

Article 77-8 (Job-seeking benefits for insured personal work performers) (1) A personal work performer shall be eligible for job-seeking benefits only when he or she satisfies all of the following requirements; provided, subparagraph 6 shall apply only to a person who was a short-term personal work performer at the time of the most recent separation from employment:
  1. The personal work performer shall have qualifying days in covered employment totaling at least 12 months during the 24-month period before the date of separation from employment;
  2. The personal work performer shall be unemployed despite their willingness and ability to work or provide personal work (including engaging in a business for profit; hereafter in this Chapter the same shall apply);
  3. The reasons for separation from employment shall not fall under any ground for restriction on eligibility for benefits under Article 58, as applied mutatis mutandis under Article 77-10(2); provided, notwithstanding subparagraph 2a of Article 58, as applied mutatis mutandis under Article 77-10(2), where the head of an employment security office determines that the personal work performer separated from employment due to a decrease in income as prescribed by Presidential Decree when the personal work performer separated from employment, the separation from employment shall not be construed as falling under any ground for restriction on eligibility for benefits under Article 58;
  4. The personal work performer shall have maintained insured status as an insured personal work performer for at least 3 months during the 24 months before the date of separation from employment;
  5. The personal work performer shall actively seek reemployment;
  6. The personal work performer shall satisfy all of the following requirements:
  a. The number of days on which the personal work performer provided personal work during the 1 month before the date of application for recognition of eligibility for benefits shall be less than 10 days, or the personal work performer shall not have provided personal work for 14 consecutive days before the date of application for recognition of eligibility for benefits;
  b. Where the personal work performer separated from employment in another business due to a reason falling under a ground for restriction on eligibility for benefits under Article 58, as applied mutatis mutandis under Article 77-10(2), during the qualifying days in covered employment in the 24 months before the date of the most recent separation from employment, the personal work performer shall have worked as a short-term personal work performer for at least 90 days during those qualifying days in covered employment.
  (2) The qualifying days in covered employment under paragraph (1)1 shall be calculated from the date of acquisition of insured status in the business related to the eligibility for benefits to the date of separation from employment, and where a person has worked as at least 2 of the following: an employee, a personal work performer, and an artist during the 24 months before the date of separation from employment, the qualifying days in covered employment shall be calculated as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) The basic daily wage for a personal work performer shall be the amount obtained by dividing the total remuneration reported under Article 16-10 of the Insurance Premium Collection Act during the 1-year period preceding the date of the most recent separation from employment related to the recognition of eligibility for benefits by the total number of days in the period serving as the basis for such calculation; provided, where the basic daily wage for a personal work performer (excluding a personal work performer who is not subject to standard remuneration under Article 3(1)2 of the Insurance Premium Collection Act) is less than the daily standard remuneration of a personal work performer under Article 3 of that Act at the time of separation from employment, the daily standard remuneration shall be the basic daily wage. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2022>
  (4) Notwithstanding paragraph (3), the basic daily wage for a personal work performer subject to the proviso of Article 48-3(3) of the Insurance Premium Collection Act shall be the amount publicly notified by the Minister of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jun. 10, 2022>
  (5) The daily amount of job-seeking benefits for a personal work performer shall be the amount obtained by multiplying the basic daily wage under paragraph (3) by 60/100. In such cases, the upper limit on the daily amount of job-seeking benefits shall be the amount prescribed by Presidential Decree, taking into consideration the upper limit on job-seeking benefits for insured employees and other relevant factors.
  (6) For a personal work performer, the 7-day period beginning on the date of reporting unemployment under Article 42 shall be regarded as a waiting period during which no job-seeking benefits shall be paid; provided, where any of the following reasons applies, a period prescribed by Presidential Decree for the applicable reason, not exceeding 4 weeks, shall be regarded as the waiting period during which no job-seeking benefits shall be paid, and where 2 or more of the following reasons apply, the longest such period shall be regarded as the waiting period: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2022>
  1. Where the separation from employment is due to a reason specified in the proviso of paragraph (1)3;
  2. Where an application for recognition of eligibility for benefits has been filed under Article 43-2(1), and the reason for the separation from employment relating to the insured status most recently lost falls under the proviso of paragraph (2) of that Article.
  (7) The period of covered employment for calculating the specified number of days for a personal work performer shall be the qualifying days in covered employment under paragraph (2); provided, in the case of a short-term personal work performer, it shall be the period calculated as prescribed by Presidential Decree in consideration of the number of days on which personal work was provided, etc. during the relevant contract period.
  (8) Notwithstanding Article 47, where the head of an employment security office pays job-seeking benefits to an insured person who is a personal work performer, the head shall pay such benefits after reducing them in whole or in part, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, in consideration of the level of income arising from employment, etc. during the period subject to recognition of unemployment, the period of work or other activities, and other relevant factors.
  [This Article Added on Jan 5, 2021]

Article 77-9 (Maternity benefits, etc. for personal work performers) (1) If an insured personal work performer or a former insured personal work performer is unable to provide personal work due to childbirth, miscarriage, or stillbirth, the Minister of Employment and Labor shall pay maternity benefits, etc.; provided, where the requirements for payment of maternity leave benefits, etc. under Article 75 and maternity benefits, etc. under Article 77-4(1) are simultaneously satisfied with respect to the same child, etc., such benefits shall be paid as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jun. 10, 2022>
  (2) The eligibility requirements, benefit levels, payment periods, etc. for maternity benefits, etc. under paragraph (1) shall be as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) Matters necessary for the application for and payment of maternity benefits, etc. under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Employment and Labor.
  [This Article Added on Jan 5, 2021]
  [Title Amended on Jun. 10, 2022]

Article 77-10 (Application mutatis mutandis) (1) Articles 13(1),14(1),15, and 17 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the insured status of a personal work performer. In such cases, "employee" shall be construed as "personal work performer"; "date of employment" as "commencement date of a contract for personal work"; and "employee who was employed" as "personal work performer whose contract for personal work has commenced".
  (2) Articles 37-2, 38, 38-2, 40(2)1, 41(2), 42, 43, 43-2, 44, 47, 48, 50, 56 through 58, and 60 through 63 shall apply mutatis mutandis to job-seeking benefits for personal work performers. In such cases, "during the 18 months before the date of separation from employment" in Article 40(2)1 shall be construed as "during t he 24 months before the date of separation from employment"; "Article 46" in the main clause of Article 63(1) shall be construed as "Article 77-3(4) and (5)"; and "Articles 47 and 49" in the former part of Article 63(5) shall be construed as "Article 47". <Amended on Dec. 31, 2022>>
  (3) Articles 62 and 73(4) shall apply mutatis mutandis to orders for return, restrictions on payment, etc. relating to maternity benefits, etc. for personal work performers. In such cases, "job-seeking benefits" in Article 62 shall be construed as "maternity benefits, etc."; "child care leave benefits" in Article 73(4) shall be construed as "maternity benefits, etc."; "child care leave" shall be construed as "childbirth, miscarriage, or stillbirth"; and "requirements for payment of child care leave benefits" shall be construed as "requirements for payment of maternity benefits, etc." <Amended on Dec. 31, 2022>
  (4) Articles 87 through 98, 99 (excluding paragraph (2)), and 100 through 112 shall apply mutatis mutandis to requests for verification of insured status, review, and further review relating to job-seeking benefits and maternity benefits, etc. for personal work performers. In such cases, "unemployment benefits under Chapter IV and child care leave benefits and maternity leave benefits, etc. under Chapter V" and "unemployment benefits under Chapter IV and child care leave benefits and maternity leave benefits, etc. under Chapter V" shall each be construed as "job-seeking benefits and maternity benefits, etc. unde r Chapter V-3"; "unemployment benefits" each as "job-seeking benefits"; "workplace" each as "workplace and office of a person required to report acquisition of insured status"; "business owner" each as "business owner and a person required to report insured status"; "employee" each as "personal work performer", "child care leave benefits, etc." as "maternity benefits, etc."; "Chapter IV" as "Chapter V-3"; "child care leave benefits, benefits for reduced working hours during the period of child care, and maternity leave benefits, etc. under Chapter V" as "maternity benefits, etc. under Chapter V-3"; and "unemployment benefits, child care leave benefits, or maternity leave benefits, etc." as "job-seeking benefits or maternity benefits, etc." <Added on Dec. 31, 2022>>
  [This Article Added on Jan 5, 2021]

CHAPTER VI EMPLOYMENT INSURANCE FUND

Article 78 (Establishment and financing of the Fund) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall establish the Employment Insurance Fund (hereinafter referred to as the "Fund") to finance insurance programs. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (2) The Fund shall be financed with insurance premiums, amounts collectible under this Act, reserves, proceeds from operation of the Fund, and other revenues.

Article 79 (Management and operation of the Fund) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall manage and operate the Fund. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (2) The National Finance Act shall apply to details relating to the management and operation of the Fund.
  (3) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall manage and operate the Fund by the following means: <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  1. Deposit with financial institutions;
  2. Deposit in treasury funds;
  3. Purchase of securities directly issued by the State, a local government, or a financial institution, or securities for which performance of obligations is guaranteed by any of the foregoing;
  4. Acquisition and disposal of real property necessary for implementing insurance programs or for increasing the assets of the Fund;
  5. Other means of increasing the assets of the Fund prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (4) When managing and operating the Fund under paragraph (1), the Minister of Employment and Labor shall ensure that earnings therefrom are at or above the level prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 80 (Use of the Fund) (1) The Fund shall be used for the following purposes: <Amended on Mar. 21, 2008; Feb. 1, 2012; Jan. 15, 2019; Jan. 5, 2021>
  1. Expenses necessary for employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs;
  2. Payment of unemployment benefits;
  2-2. Support for National Pension contributions under Article 55-2;
  3. Payment of child care leave benefits and maternity leave benefits, etc.;
  4. Refund of insurance premiums;
  5. Repayments of temporary borrowings and payment of interest thereon;
  6. Contributions to persons who perform business affairs under this Act and the Insurance Premium Collection Act on behalf of another person or are entrusted with such business affairs;
  7. Other expenses prescribed by Presidential Decree as necessary for enforcing this Act, and expenses incidental to the implementation of the programs under subparagraphs 1 and 2.
  (2) The amount contributed from the Fund to the National Health Insurance Service under Article 13 of the National Health Insurance Act in accordance with paragraph (1)6 shall be calculated based on the proportion accounted for by collection affairs (referring to notice, receipt, and delinquency management affairs), and other relevant factors. <Added on Jan. 15, 2019>
  (3) Matters necessary for the criteria for payment, use, and management of contributions under paragraph (1)6 shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added on Mar. 21, 2008; Jan. 15, 2019>

Article 81 (Fund operation plan) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall prepare a fund operation plan each year and obtain approval thereof from the President, following deliberation by the Employment Insurance Committee under Article 7 and the State Council. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2008; Jun. 4, 2010>
  (2) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall publish the results of operation of the Fund each year following deliberation by the Employment Insurance Committee under Article 7. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2008; Jun. 4, 2010>

Article 82 (Opening of Fund account) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall open an account for the Employment Insurance Fund with the Bank of Korea. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (2) The account for the Employment Insurance Fund under paragraph (1) shall be managed separately for employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs, unemployment benefits, employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs for self-employed persons, and unemployment benefits for self-employed persons. <Amended on Jul. 21, 2011>

Article 83 (Receipt and disbursement of the Fund) Matters necessary for the receipt and disbursement of the Fund in managing and operating the Fund shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 84 (Accumulation of the Fund) (1) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall accumulate surplus funds as reserve funds to prepare for mass unemployment and other instability in employment conditions. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (2) The appropriate amount of surplus funds under paragraph (1) shall be as follows:
  1. Year-end reserves in the account for employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs: At least 1 time but less than 1.5 times the expenditures for the relevant year;
  2. Year-end reserves in the unemployment benefits account: At least 1.5 times but less than 2 times the expenditures for the relevant year.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 2008]

Article 85 (Disposition of surpluses and deficits) (1) Any surplus arising from the settlement of accounts of the Fund shall be accumulated as reserves.
  (2) Any deficit arising from the settlement of accounts of the Fund may be covered by using reserves.

Article 86 (Borrowings) The Fund may borrow money from financial institutions, other funds, or other sources at the expense of the Fund if a shortage of funds occur or is expected to occur when expenditures are made from the Fund.

CHAPTER VII REQUESTS FOR REVIEW AND FURTHER REVIEW

Article 87 (Review and further review) (1) A person who is dissatisfied with verification of the acquisition or loss of insured status under Article 17 or a disposition regarding unemployment benefits under Chapter IV or child care leave benefits and maternity leave benefits, etc. under Chapter V (hereinafter referred to as "initial disposition, etc.") may file a request for review with an examiner under Article 89, and a person who is dissatisfied with the relevant decision may file a request for further review with the Board of Review under Article 99. <Amended on Feb. 1, 2012>
  (2) A request for review under paragraph (1) shall be filed within 90 days after the date on which the applicant becomes aware of the verification or disposition under that paragraph, and a request for further review shall be filed within 90 days after the date on which the applicant becomes aware of the decision on the request for review.
  (3) A request for review or further review under paragraph (1) shall be deemed a judicial claim with respect to interruption of prescription.

Article 88 (Appointment of agent) An applicant for review or further review may appoint any of the following persons as his or her agent, in addition to a legal representative:
  1. The spouse, a lineal ascendant or descendant, or a sibling of the applicant;
  2. An executive officer or employee of a corporation, where the applicant is a corporation;
  3. An attorney-at-law or certified labor consultant;
  4. A person permitted by the Board or Review under Article 99.

Article 89 (Employment Insurance Examiner) (1) Employment Insurance Examiners (hereinafter referred to as "examiners") shall be assigned to conduct reviews under Article 87.
  (2) Upon receipt of a request for review under Article 87(1), an examiner shall make a decision on the request within 30 days; provided, where the examiner is unable to make a decision within that period due to unavoidable circumstances, the period may be extended once by up to 10 days. <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (3) Matters necessary for the authorized number, qualifications, assignment, and duties of examiners shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (4) If there are circumstances that make it difficult to expect a fair review and decision from an examiner, a party may file an application with the Minister of Employment and Labor to challenge the examiner. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (5) Where an applicant for review dies, if the applicant was entitled to unemployment benefits, a surviving family member under Article 57 shall succeed to the status of the applicant for review; in any other case, the heir or a person who succeeds to a right or interest relating to the initial disposition, etc. that is the subject of the request for review shall succeed to the status of the applicant for review.

Article 90 (Request for review) (1) If a request for review is filed under Article 87(1), a request for review of verification of the acquisition or loss of insured status under Article 17 shall be filed with an examiner through the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service under Article 10 of the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service"), and a request for review of a disposition regarding unemployment benefits under Chapter IV or child care leave benefits and maternity leave benefits, etc. under Chapter V shall be filed with an examiner through the head of an employment security office. <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019>
  (2) The head of an employment security office or the Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service shall, within 5 days after receiving a written request for review, forward the request to the examiner together with a written opinion. <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019>

Article 91 (Manner of filing) All requests for review shall be filed in writing, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 92 (Rectification and dismissal without prejudice) (1) An examiner shall dismiss a request for review without prejudice by decision where the period prescribed in Article 87(2) has expired or where the request for review has been filed in violation of the manner prescribed by statutes or regulations and cannot be rectified.
  (2) Where a request for review is filed in violation of the manner prescribed by statutes or regulations but can be rectified, an examiner may order the applicant for review to rectify the request for review within a reasonable period specified by the examiner; provided, where the matter to be rectified is minor, the examiner may rectify it ex officio.
  (3) Where an applicant for review fails to rectify the request for review within the period specified under paragraph (2), an examiner shall dismiss the request for review without prejudice by decision.

Article 93 (Stay of execution of initial disposition, etc.) (1) The filing of a request for review shall not stay the execution of the initial disposition, etc.; provided, where an examiner deems that there is an urgent need to prevent serious harm that may result from the execution of the initial disposition, etc., the examiner may stay the execution ex officio.
  (2) Where an examiner intends to stay execution under the proviso of paragraph (1), the examiner shall notify the head of the employment security office or the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service thereof in writing, stating the reasons therefor. <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019>
  (3) Upon receipt of a notice under paragraph (2), the head of the employment security office or the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service shall stay the execution without delay. <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019>
  (4) Where an examiner stays the execution under paragraph (2), the examiner shall, without delay, notify the applicant for review thereof in writing.

Article 94 (Authority of examiners) (1) Where an examiner deems it necessary for proceedings on a request for review, the examiner may, upon application by the applicant for review or ex officio, conduct any of the following investigations:
  1. Requiring the applicant for review or any relevant person to appear at a designated place to answer questions or state opinions;
  2. Requiring the applicant for review or any relevant person to submit documents and other articles that may constitute evidence;
  3. Having a third party with specialized knowledge or experience conduct an appraisal;
  4. Entering a workplace or any other place related to the case to question the business owner, employees, or other relevant persons, or to inspect documents and other articles.
  (2) When conducting questioning and inspections under paragraph (1)4, examiners shall carry identification verifying their authority and present it to the relevant persons.

Article 95 (Reimbursement for actual expenses) A person who appears at a designated place under Article 94(1)1 and an appraiser who conducts an appraisal under Article 94(1)3 shall be reimbursed for actual expenses determined by the Minister of Employment and Labor. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010; May 26, 2020>

Article 96 (Decision) Upon completion of the proceedings on a request for review, an examiner shall revoke all or part of the initial disposition, etc. or dismiss all or part of the request for review.

Article 97 (Form of decision) (1) A decision under Article 89 shall be made in writing, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) Upon making a decision, an examiner shall send an authentic copy of the decision to the applicant for review and the head of the employment security office or the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service that made the initial disposition, etc. <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019>

Article 98 (Effect of decision) (1) A decision shall take effect on the date on which an authentic copy of the decision is sent to the applicant for review and to the head of the employment security office or the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service. <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019>
  (2) A decision shall bind the head of the employment security office or the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service that rendered the initial disposition, etc. <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019>

Article 99 (Employment Insurance Appeal Committee) (1) The Employment Insurance Appeal Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Appeal Committee") shall be established within the Ministry of Employment and Labor to conduct further reviews under Article 87. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (2) The Appeal Committee shall be composed of not more than 15 members, including at least 1 representative of employees and at least 1 representative of employers. <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (3) Of the members under paragraph (2), 2 shall be standing members.
  (4) None of the following persons shall be appointed as a member of the Appeal Committee: <Amended on Jan. 20, 2015; May 26, 2020; Jun. 10, 2022>
  1. A person under adult guardianship or limited guardianship, or a person declared bankrupt and not yet reinstated;
  2. A person for whom 3 years have not elapsed since his or her imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment declared by a court was completely executed (including where the execution is deemed to have been completed) or exempted;
  3. A person who is under suspension of the execution of his or her imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment declared by a court.
  (5) A member who is not a public official may be removed from office if he or she falls under any of the following subparagraphs: <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019>
  1. Where the member becomes unable to perform his or her duties due to a mental or physical disability;
  2. Where the member has committed misconduct in connection with his or her duties;
  3. Where the member is deemed unsuitable to serve as a member due to neglect of duties, conduct detrimental to the dignity of the office, or any other reason;
  4. Where the member indicates that he or she is unable to perform his or her duties.
  (6) Standing members shall not join any political party or engage in political activities.
  (7) Upon receipt of a request for further review under Article 87(1), the Appeal Committee shall render an adjudication within 50 days. In such cases, Article 89(2) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the extension of the adjudication.
  (8) A secretariat shall be established in the Appeal Committee.
  (9) Matters necessary for the organization, operation, etc. of the Appeal Committee and its secretariat shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 100 (Respondent in further review) The respondent to a request for further review shall be the head of the employment security office or the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service that made the initial disposition, etc. <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019>

Article 101 (Proceedings) (1) Upon receipt of a request for further review, the Appeal Committee shall set the date and place for proceedings on the request and notify the parties and the examiner who reviewed the case of the date and place at least 3 days before the date of the proceedings.
  (2) The parties may state their opinions to the Appeal Committee in writing or orally.
  (3) Proceedings on requests for further review before the Appeal Committee shall be open to the public; provided, they may be closed to the public upon request by both parties or either party.
  (4) The Appeal Committee shall prepare records of proceedings.
  (5) A party or relevant person may request access to the records of proceedings under paragraph (4).
  (6) The Appeal Committee shall not refuse a request for access filed by a party or relevant person under paragraph (5) without good cause.
  (7) Articles 94 and 95 shall apply mutatis mutandis to proceedings on requests for further review. In such cases, "examiner" shall be construed as "Appeal Committee"; "request for review" shall be construed as "request for further review"; and "applicant for review" shall be construed as "applicant for further review".

Article 102 (Provisions applicable mutatis mutandis) Articles 89(4) and (5), 91 through 93, and 96 through 98 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Appeal Committee and further review. In such cases, "examiner" in Article 89(4) shall be construed as "member of the Appeal Committee"; "decision" in Articles 89(4), 97, and 98 as "adjudication"; "request for review" in Articles 91, 93, and 96 as "request for further review"; "examiner" in Articles 93, 96, and 97 as "Appeal Committee"; and "applicant for review" in Articles 93, 97, and 98 as "applicant for further review"..

Article 103 (Notice) If the head of an employment security office or the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service makes an initial disposition, etc. or an examiner sends an authentic copy of a decision under Article 97(2), the head of the employment security office, the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service, or the examiner, as applicable, shall inform the other party or the applicant for review whether a request for review or further review may be filed regarding the initial disposition, etc. or decision and, where such request is filed, of the procedures for filing the request through the relevant agency and the filing period. <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019>

Article 104 (Relationship to other statutes) (1) In applying Article 18 of the Administrative Litigation Act, an adjudication on a request for further review shall be construed as an adjudication on an administrative appeal.
  (2) The Administrative Appeals Act shall apply to matters relating to requests for review and further review that are not provided in this Act.

CHAPTER VIII SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 105 (Prohibition of disadvantageous treatment) A business owner shall not dismiss or otherwise subject an employee to disadvantageous treatment on the grounds that the employee has filed a request for verification under Article 17.

Article 106 (Application mutatis mutandis) Articles 27, 27-2, 27-3, 28, 28-2 through 28-7, 29, 29-2, 29-3, 30, 32,3 9, 41, and 42 of the Insurance Premium Collection Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the collection of the following amounts collectible under this Act: <Amended on Jul. 21, 2011>>
  1. Refunds of assistance provided for employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs or additional amounts collectible;
  2. Refunds of unemployment benefits or additional amounts collectible;
  3. Refunds of child care leave benefits, etc. or additional amounts collectible.

Article 107 (Extinctive prescription) (1) The following rights shall be extinguished by prescription if not exercised for 3 years: <Amended on Jan. 15, 2019>
  1. The right to receive or obtain a refund of subsidies under Chapter III;
  2. The right to receive or obtain a refund of employment promotion allowances under Chapter IV;
  3. The right to obtain a refund of job-seeking benefits under Chapter IV;
  4. The right to obtain a refund of child care leave benefits, benefits for reduced working hours during periods of child care, and maternity leave benefits, etc. under Chapter V.
  (2) Article 113 of the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the interruption of extinctive prescription. <Amended on Jan. 20, 2015>

Article 108 (Reporting) (1) If the Minister of Employment and Labor deems it necessary for enforcing this Act, including verifying insured status and investigating improper receipt of benefits, the Minister may require a business owner who employs or employed an insured person or eligible recipient, an agency handling insurance affairs under Article 33 of the Insurance Premium Collection Act (hereinafter referred to as an "agency handling insurance affairs"), or a person who was such an agency to submit reports or relevant documents, or to have a relevant person appear. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010; Jan. 5, 2021>
  (2) A person separated from employment may request the former business owner or an agency handling insurance affairs entrusted by that business owner to issue a certificate necessary to receive unemployment benefits. In such cases, the business owner or the agency handling insurance affairs upon receipt of such request shall issue the certificate. <Amended on May 26, 2020>
  (3) The Minister of Employment and Labor may require an insured person, an eligible recipient, or a claimant for payment of unpaid unemployment benefits to submit reports necessary for enforcing this Act, including verifying insured status and investigating improper receipt of benefits, or to submit relevant documents or appear in person. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010; May 26, 2020>

Article 109 (Investigation) (1) If the Minister of Employment and Labor deems it necessary for enforcing this Act, including verifying insured status and investigating improper receipt of benefits, the Minister may require public officials under his or her jurisdiction to enter the workplace of a business owner who employs or employed an insured person or eligible recipient, or the office of an agency handling insurance affairs or a person who was such an agency, to question relevant persons or inspect books and other documents. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (2) Where the Minister of Employment and Labor conducts an investigation under paragraph (1), the Minister shall notify the business owner, etc. in advance of matters necessary for the investigation, such as the date, time, and details of the investigation; provided, this shall not apply where the investigation is urgent or where the Minister deems that prior notice would make it impossible to achieve the purpose of the investigation. <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>
  (3) Public officials conducting an investigation under paragraph (1) shall carry identification verifying their authority and present it to relevant persons.
  (4) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall notify the business owner, etc., in writing, of the results of the investigation conducted under paragraph (1). <Amended on Jun. 4, 2010>

  (2) If necessary to perform the affairs under paragraph (1)3-2 and 4 through 11, the Minister of Employment and Labor may request the head of the competent tax office to provide the following tax information by means of a document stating the taxpayer’s personal information and the purpose of use: <Amended on Jan. 5, 2021>

CHAPTER IX PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 116 (Penalty provisions) (1) A person who conspires with a business owner and receives any of the following subsidies or benefits by fraud or other improper means, and the business owner who conspires with that person, shall each be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 5 years or by a fine not exceeding 50 million won: <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020; Jan. 5, 2021>
  1. Subsidies for employment stabilization and vocational skills development programs under Chapter III;
  2. Unemployment benefits under Chapter IV;
  3. Child care leave benefits, benefits for reduced working hours during periods of child care, and maternity leave benefits, etc. under Chapter V;
  4. Job-seeking benefits and maternity benefits, etc. under Chapters V-2 and V-3.
  (2) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 3 years or by a fine not exceeding 30 million won: <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020; Jan. 5, 2021; Dec. 31, 2022>
  1. A business owner who dismisses or otherwise subjects an employee to disadvantageous treatment, in violation of Article 105 (including cases where Article 15 applies mutatis mutandis under Articles 77-5(3) and (4) and 77-10(3) and (4));
  2. A person who receives subsidies or benefits under any of the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) by fraud or other improper means; provided, this shall not apply to cases falling under paragraph (1).
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Aug. 27, 2019]

Article 117 (Joint penalty provisions) If the representative of a corporation or an agent or employee of, or any other person employed by, the corporation or an individual commits any violation under Article 116 in conducting the business affairs of the corporation or individual, the corporation or individual shall be punished by a fine prescribed in the relevant provisions; provided, this shall not apply where such corporation or individual has not neglected to exercise due care and supervision over the relevant business affairs to prevent such violation.
